# Agent Art 1.0.0: full reference for AI agents

> Game art and audio for AI agents: MCP server + live web UI for pixel-art sprites, rigs and animations, tilesets, textures, low-poly 3D models (.glb), combat effects, planets, sound effects and music.

Generated by scripts/build-llms.js from src/mcp.js (server instructions and tool schemas), src/docs.js (art_help topics and draw commands) and src/skills.js (skills). Do not edit by hand: run `npm run docs:llms`.
Package: @rusticstack/agent-art (npm). Repository: https://github.com/RusticStack/agent-art. Install for Claude Code: claude mcp add agent-art -s user -- npx -y @rusticstack/agent-art mcp

Contents: 1. MCP server instructions; 2. Tools (29); 3. Draw commands (art_draw ops); 4. Help topics (23); 5. Skills (21).

## 1. MCP server instructions

Agent Art: pixel-art editor for agents (sprites, tiles, textures, icons, UI, animations, 2.5D scenes, game assets). The user watches live in a web UI (art_open_ui).
Workflow: palette ramps first (art_palette ramp) -> flat silhouettes -> shade (auto form shading) -> outline -> hand detail (grid) -> art_critique -> fix -> art_view.
Multi-asset work: art_project create (shared palette + style notes), review with art_sheet. Any character/creature with more than one view or frame: use art_rig (template:"humanoid"|"humanoid_hd" (detailed 64x96+)|"blob"|"flyer" is fastest; templates are only defaults) instead of hand-drawing frames, so every frame stays the same asset. Several characters sharing motion: art_anim (skeleton + clip library + skins + batch to game strips).
3D (HD-2D maps, props -> .glb): art_model. Planets, ground terrain, skyboxes, asteroid fields: art_planet. First-person arms + gun/attachment sweeps: art_fp. Combat effects (muzzle flashes, impacts, decals, explosions): art_fx.
Audio (SFX, music, mixing; you cannot hear, so read analyze/critique reports): art_audio.
The user leaves review notes on assets in the web UI: art_review list (replies say when the asset you touch has open notes).
Retire superseded art with art_cleanup (plan -> apply; soft delete to a trash, restore undoes it).
Orient yourself with art_graph (summary / query: what is part of what, a few hundred chars) instead of art_info on everything; record relations with art_graph link / group / tag / note.
Details on demand: art_help {topic: workflow|textures|characters|animation|scenes|hires|minecraft|rig|library|skin2d|melee|3d|materials|damage|audio|music|mixing|perception|planets|fx|fp|graph|cleanup}, {op:"<draw command>"} or {skill} (recipes).

## 2. Tools

Every tool takes one JSON object. Tools with an "action" parameter dispatch on it. Keys outside the schema are passed through to the engine too: the nested options are documented in the tool description and in art_help.

### art_create_canvas

Create a canvas (transparent unless background). frames>1 = animation strip of equal frames. project = inherit its palette.

Parameters:
- name (string, required)
- width (integer): default 16
- height (integer): frame height (default width)
- frames (integer)
- background (string)
- palette (object)
- project (string)
- meta (object): e.g. {"texture":"blocks/stone"}
- overwrite (boolean)

### art_list

List canvases (optionally of a project), projects and the UI URL. Relations and groups: art_graph.

Parameters:
- project (string)

### art_info

Canvas details (summary): size, frames, layers, animations, meta keys, colour count. full:true = everything (palette, meta, frame lists); fields:[..] = only those fields in full.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- color_limit (integer)
- full (boolean)
- fields (array of string)

### art_draw

Run drawing commands on a canvas as ONE atomic undo step. commands: [{"op":"rect","x":0,"y":0,"w":4,"h":4,"color":"#c33"}, ...] (each name{fields} below is {"op":"name", fields}). Pixels, origin top-left. Colors: #rgb #rrggbb #rrggbbaa, rgb(), hsl(), "transparent" or a palette key.
Every command may set: layer, frame (frame-local coords), mask ("opaque" | "transparent" | color | "!<color>" | "layer:<name>" | "!layer:<name>"), blend ("replace" | "over"), symmetry ("x"|"y"|"xy").
SHAPES: grid{x?,y?,rows:[str],legend?,cpp?} pixels{points:[[x,y,color?]],color?} line{x1,y1,x2,y2|points,color,width?,pixel_perfect?} curve{points:[3|4 pts],color,width?} polygon{points,color?,outline?,fill?} rect{x,y,w,h,color?,outline?,fill?,thickness?} ellipse{x,y,w,h,color?,outline?,fill?,thickness?} fill{x,y,color,tolerance?,contiguous?} text{x,y,text,color,font?,scale?,align?,shadow?}
FORM/SURFACE: shade{colors:[dark..light],light?,of?,depth?,profile?,per_color?,region} cells{colors:[dark..light],gap_color?,size?,gap?,layout?,stretch?,seed?,region} noise{colors,weights?,scale?,octaves?,despeckle?,seed?,region} scatter{colors|color,density?|count,size?,seed?,region} outline{color,mode?,of?,from_layer?,diagonal?,region} bevel{light?,dark?,size?,region} damage{amount?,seed?,kinds?,on?,palette?,mirror?,region}
COLOR: replace{from,to,tolerance?,region} remap{map:{from:to},tolerance?,region} gradient{colors,direction?,dither?,region} adjust{hue?,saturation?,lightness?,jitter?,alpha?,region} quantize{colors?,dither?,alpha_threshold?,region}
TRANSFORM: copy{x,y,w,h,to_x,to_y,from_canvas?,from_layer?,from_frame?,scale?,flip_x?,tint?,opacity?} flip{axis,region} rotate{turns|angle,expand?,region} shift{dx,dy,wrap?,region} mirror{axis,source} clear{region?}
LIGHT: light{x,y,radius,color,intensity?,mode?,steps?} fog{color,from?,to?,direction?,noise?,steps?,region} rays{x,y,angle,spread,count,width,color,alpha?} glow{threshold?,radius?,intensity?,gain?,normalize?,wrap?} blur{radius,region} vignette{strength?,radius?,color?} cast_shadow{from_layer,dx,dy,color,squash?,skew?,soft?}
ISO: iso_box{at:[gx,gy,gz]|x,y,tile,origin,w|size_left/right,height,top,left?,right?,outline?,edge?,anchor?,inset?} iso_tile{same as iso_box without height,color}
region = x?,y?,w?,h?. art_help {op:"<name>"} = full options + example; errors include usage.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- commands (array of object)
- commands_file (string)
- layer (string|integer): name or index (default active)
- frame (integer)
- label (string): shown in the UI log
- preview (boolean): also return an image of the result
- critique (boolean): also return the art_critique summary

### art_view

See the canvas as an image (checker = transparent; grid when zoomed). tile:3 = seam check; frame+onion for animation; x,y,w,h zooms; big canvases come back as a downsampled overview.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- scale (integer)
- max_size (integer): default 512 px
- tile (integer)
- grid (boolean)
- layer (string|integer): name or index (default active)
- frame (integer)
- onion (integer)
- background (string)
- guide (string): "grid:16", "iso:32", "center"
- tint (string)
- apply_tint (boolean)
- x (integer)
- y (integer)
- w (integer)
- h (integer)

### art_critique

Automatic pixel-art review: noise/stray pixels, contrast, color count, tiling seams, outline, pillow shading, jaggies, and animation consistency (size drift, ground line, palette drift). Returns issues with coordinates and fixes. Use after drawing, before exporting.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- kind (string): one of auto | texture | sprite | scene
- frame (integer)
- animation (string)
- style (enum): one of auto | lowres | hd
- layer (string|integer): name or index (default active)
- tileable (boolean)
- max_colors (integer)
- all_frames (boolean)

### art_help

Docs on demand: {op:"shade"} = draw op options + example; {topic} = guide (long ones answer with a core + section index: {topic, section:"a,b"} or full:true); {skill} = step-by-step recipe.

Parameters:
- op (string)
- topic (string): one of index | ops | workflow | textures | characters | animation | scenes | hires | minecraft | rig | library | skin2d | melee | 3d | materials | damage | audio | music | mixing | perception | planets | fx | fp | graph | cleanup
- section (string)
- full (boolean)
- skill (string): one of list | tileable-texture | sprite | rig | rig-hd | weapon-handling | anim-library | walk-cycle | iso-scene | hd2d-scene | minecraft-pack | 3d-kit | ship-model | hard-surface | ships-structures | fp-weapon | prop-rig | ui-icons | sfx-pack | music-track | planets-space | combat-fx

### art_sheet

Many canvases in one labelled image (project, list or name regex) to review a set for consistency.

Parameters:
- project (string)
- canvases (array of string)
- filter (string): regex on name
- exclude (string)
- texture_filter (string): regex on meta.texture
- scale (integer)
- cell (integer)
- tile (integer)
- apply_tint (boolean)
- show_texture (boolean)
- columns (integer)
- labels (boolean)
- limit (integer)
- offset (integer)

### art_project

Projects group canvases (sprite set, tileset, pack) with a shared palette and style notes. create {name, palette?, notes?, meta?}; update {name, notes?|append_notes?, meta?}; list; info {name}; delete {name, delete_canvases?}.

Parameters:
- action (string, required): one of create | update | list | info | delete
- name (string)
- description (string)
- notes (string)
- append_notes (string)
- palette (object)
- meta (object)
- delete_canvases (boolean)
- overwrite (boolean)

### art_read

Exact pixels of a region as text rows + legend (the format art_draw grid accepts). Max 128x128; read small regions.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- x (integer)
- y (integer)
- w (integer)
- h (integer)
- layer (string|integer): name or index (default active)
- frame (integer)

### art_palette

Palette (canvas, or project:<name> for the shared one). Keys work anywhere a color does; 1-char keys work in grid rows. ramp {base, steps?:5, prefix|keys} = hue-shifted shading ramp dark->light.

Parameters:
- canvas (string)
- project (string)
- action (string, required): one of get | set | remove | clear | ramp
- colors (object)
- keys (array of string)
- base (string)
- steps (integer)
- prefix (string)
- hue_shift (number)
- spread (number)
- saturation_shift (number)

### art_layer

Layers. add {name, position?: above|below|top|bottom, blend?, opacity?, select?}, remove, select, rename, visibility, opacity, blend, move {index|position}, duplicate, merge_down, flatten {keep_hidden|discard_hidden}, stamp_visible (composite of visible layers -> new top layer).

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- action (string, required): one of add | remove | select | rename | visibility | opacity | blend | move | duplicate | merge_down | flatten | stamp_visible
- layer (string|integer): name or index (default active)
- name (string)
- index (integer)
- position (string): one of above | below | top | bottom
- blend (string): one of normal | multiply | screen | add | overlay | darken | lighten | soft-light
- opacity (number)
- visible (boolean)
- select (boolean)
- keep_hidden (boolean)
- discard_hidden (boolean)
- hide_others (boolean)
- keep_visible (boolean)

### art_canvas

Canvas changes: meta (merge; null deletes), delete, duplicate {new_name}, resize {width,height,anchor}, scale {factor|width,height, method: nearest|scale2x (clean pixel-art upscale)}, crop, set_frames {frame_height}, add_frame, normal_map.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- action (string, required): one of meta | delete | duplicate | resize | scale | crop | set_frames | add_frame | normal_map
- new_name (string)
- meta (object)
- project (string)
- width (integer)
- height (integer)
- anchor (string)
- factor (number)
- method (string): one of nearest | scale2x
- x (integer)
- y (integer)
- w (integer)
- h (integer)
- frame_height (integer)
- copy_from (integer)
- strength (number)
- bevel (integer)
- overwrite (boolean)

### art_animation

Frame strip animation. list; tag {name, from,to|frames, duration|durations|fps, loop?, direction?}; untag; insert {at?, count?, copy_from?}; duplicate {frame, to?}; move {frame, to}; delete {frame|frames}; set_frame_size; filmstrip {animation?} (image of all frames); export {format: gif|spritesheet|frames, animation?, scale?, path? (absolute, ./ = server cwd, bare = workspace exports), layout?: rows (one row per tag) | strip | files (one strip per tag), json?:false}.

Parameters:
- canvas (string, required)
- action (string, required): one of list | tag | untag | insert | duplicate | move | delete | set_frame_size | filmstrip | export
- name (string)
- frames (array of integer)
- from (integer)
- to (integer)
- frame (integer)
- at (integer)
- count (integer)
- copy_from (integer)
- duration (integer)
- durations (array of integer)
- fps (number)
- loop (boolean)
- direction (string): one of forward | reverse | pingpong
- frame_height (integer)
- animation (string)
- onion (integer)
- scale (integer)
- format (string): one of gif | spritesheet | frames
- path (string)
- layout (string): one of rows | strip | files
- json (boolean)

### art_rig

Rigs: parts drawn once per view, poses tweened into frames, so a character stays identical across views and animations. Fastest: create {name, frame, template:"humanoid"|"humanoid_hd" (64x96+, 8 directions, IK)|"blob"|"flyer"} (override/add/remove parts, views, poses, presets), draw the cells, animate {preset, view}. Custom: create {name, frame, views?, mirror?, parts:{p:{w,h,pivot,parent?,at?,z?,variants?,views?:{view:{at,z,hidden,pivot}}}}, root?, sampling?, secondary?:{part:{stiffness,damping}}, scale_children?}; info; update; templates; pose {pose, parts:{p:{x,y,rot,sx,sy,variant,hide}}, views?:{view:{p:{..}}}, ik?:{end:{target:[x,y]|{part,at},bend?,rot?}}, from?}; preview; turnaround; animate {preset} or {animation, view, keys:[{pose|parts,t?,ease?,mirror_pairs?}], frames, fps, loop?, plant?, secondary?, plant_feet?, canvas?, only?/hide?, variant?}. Held weapons: weapon:{class, attachments?} (carry states, hands locked on grips; animate carry?/constraints?; check = validate every clip+view; layers/explain = draw order; debug_render = per-part atlas of a frame). depth:true = arm order from depth per frame (split parts, z keys {z:{part:n}}); zcheck = flicker/order; consistency = views agree; derive {from, to} copies cells; animate stable?, events?. 2D skinning: skin {skin:{<mesh>:{part|canvas, absorb?, bones?, method?, paint?, shapes?}}} bends drawn sprites (crisp, same palette); weights {mesh?, bone?} = check + heat map; shapes {mesh, shapes}; chain {part, bones?} = cable/strap; export {layers?, path?}; constrain, limits, ik chain:n (CCD). info/create/update reply in summary (full:true). Library (skeletons/clips/skins/batch): art_anim. art_help {topic:"rig"}.

Parameters:
- action (string, required): one of create | info | update | pose | preview | animate | turnaround | templates | check | layers | explain | debug_render | consistency | derive | zcheck | skin | weights | shapes | chain | export
- tag (string)
- all_frames (boolean)
- name (string)
- part_a (string)
- part_b (string)
- depth (boolean|object)
- stable (boolean|object)
- events (array of object)
- to (array|string)
- flip (boolean)
- weapon (object|boolean)
- carry (string|object)
- attach (array of string)
- variant (string|array)
- variant_sets (object)
- constraints (enum): one of refuse | fix | warn | off
- clips (array of string)
- visibility (boolean)
- full (boolean)
- fields (array of string)
- template (string): one of humanoid | humanoid_hd | blob | flyer
- preset (string)
- presets (object)
- poses (object)
- plant_feet (boolean)
- plant (boolean|array)
- secondary (boolean|object)
- ik (object)
- sampling (string): one of nearest8 | rotsprite | smooth
- scale_children (boolean)
- feet (array)
- only (array of string)
- hide (array of string)
- skin (object|null)
- mesh (string)
- bone (string)
- shapes (object)
- constrain (array of object)
- limits (object)
- part (string)
- layers (boolean)
- path (string)
- ik_from (object): {canvas, animation?, map:{hand_f:"socket_grip_r"}} per-frame IK targets
- frame (array of integer|integer)
- views (array|object)
- mirror (object)
- parts (object)
- root (array of number)
- pairs (array)
- project (string)
- palette (object)
- pose (string)
- from (string)
- merge (boolean)
- view (string)
- scale (integer)
- animation (string)
- keys (array of object)
- frames (integer)
- fps (number)
- duration (integer)
- loop (boolean)
- direction (string): one of forward | reverse | pingpong
- canvas (string)
- overwrite (boolean)

### art_anim

Animation library: author motion once per skeleton, render many skins. skeleton {name, template:"humanoid_hd", frame, weapon?, proportions?} (+ standard clips); clip {skeleton, name, keys?|layers?:[{clip, mask?, weight?, additive?}], frames, fps, events?}; skin {name, skeleton, proportions?, equipment?, loadouts?} (creates the rig to draw); retarget {clip, from, to}; render {skin, clip, view}; batch {skins, clips?, views?, out, pad?:"auto", front?:"auto", weapon?:"runtime"} = game strips + manifest (runtime: gun-free + sockets); gltf {skin}; list; info. Guns: weapon {name, class, skin}, conform, weapon_sheet {weapon, out}, composite {skin, weapon, clip, view}, weapon_check {skin}. Melee: melee {skeleton, weapon?:"combat_knife"|.., shield?, disarm?:"take"|"drop" (gun skeletons)} = strikes/blocks/reactions/paired takedowns + hit events/volumes; melee_check; melee_sheet {weapons?, out}; paired {skin, victim_skin?, pair, view?} (art_help melee). art_help {topic:"library"}.

Parameters:
- action (string, required): one of skeleton | clip | skin | retarget | render | batch | gltf | list | info | weapon | conform | weapon_sheet | composite | weapon_check | melee | melee_check | melee_sheet | paired
- name (string)
- skeleton (string)
- template (string)
- frame (array of integer)
- weapon (object|boolean|string)
- shield (boolean)
- disarm (string): one of take | drop
- pair (string)
- victim_skin (string)
- tolerance (number)
- class (string)
- weapons (array of string)
- from_skin (string)
- attachments (object)
- points (object)
- fix (boolean)
- pitch (array of number)
- attach (array|string)
- select (array of integer)
- max_size (integer)
- from_rig (string)
- preset (string)
- proportions (object|string)
- masks (object)
- depth (boolean|object)
- clips (array|string|boolean)
- keys (array of object)
- frames (integer)
- fps (number)
- loop (boolean)
- events (array of object)
- layers (array of object)
- mask (string|array|object)
- additive (boolean)
- ref (object)
- plant (boolean|array)
- secondary (boolean|object)
- carry (string|object)
- delete (boolean)
- skin (string)
- skins (array of string)
- rig (string)
- parts (object)
- variant_sets (object)
- equipment (object)
- loadouts (object|array|string)
- loadout (string)
- clip (string)
- from (string)
- to (string)
- map (object)
- view (string)
- views (array|string)
- canvas (string)
- out (string)
- manifest (string)
- pad (string|number|array)
- front (string|array)
- stable (boolean|object)
- max_width (integer)
- order (boolean)
- path (string)
- full (boolean)
- overwrite (boolean)
- project (string)

### art_model

3D low-poly models textured with pixel art (HD-2D, nearest filter) -> glTF .glb. Units px (32 px = 1 unit). create {name, parts:[{type, ...args, at?:[x,y,z], cell?:[gx,gy,gz] (x grid), turn?:0-3, rotate?:[x,y,z]deg (X,Y,Z about origin or pivot?), scale?, mirror?, array?:{count, step|cell_step, turn?, rotate?, about?}, opacity?|glass?, name?, parent?}]}. Rigs (art_help 3d): name/parent parts = nodes (pivot = joint), sockets, template:fp_arms|fp_rifle|fp_pistol; pose {pose, parts:{<part>:{rot,at}}}; animate {clip, keys:[{pose|parts,t}], events?}; preview {pose|clip, view:fp|side}; render {canvas, pose|clip, camera, size:[w,h], sweep?, quantize?, outline?, only?|hide?, hold?} = sprites + socket anchors. Guns: weapon:true (hold:{weapon} on arms = hands on grips per carry state; check validates). Kit: floor wall corner pillar column arch vault stairs ledge balustrade roof rubble box (taper|bevel|insets) wedge inset cylinder (r_top/r_bottom, wrap) cone plane shape loft; props: extrude lathe; layout: model (place other models). texture|faces{top,front,..}|side|top|color; world UVs, seamless across pieces. Ruins: broken, holes:<mask>. overlays:[{texture,where:bottom|top|corners|edges}]. ctm {name:<new canvas>, ctm:{base, method:full|compact|horizontal|vertical|random|repeat|overlay, border?}} = connected textures. update {name, parts|add|set:{i:{..}}|remove:[i]}; info; list; delete; preview {name, views?, size?, ao?, lod?, morph?} (game = 38° camera); export {name, path?, instances?, atlas?, up?:"z", normal_maps?, bake_ao?, lods?:[1,0.5,0.2], impostor?, collision?, occluder?, stats?}. Hard-surface: tube {path|from,to,sag}, greeble (or box greebles:[{face}]), part material, bump, trim:"sheet:strip" (trim {canvas} = sheet), boolean, merge, morphs, cull. Skinning: skeleton {skeleton:{template|from_parts|library}}, skin {skin:{method, paint?, shapes?}}, weights, animate {bones|retarget}, export {profile:"roblox"}. Materials v2 (art_help materials): material {name, material, preset|set}; presets painted_hull brushed_metal glass_canopy cloth neon skin; light parts; displace; export {profile:three|roblox|minimal, lightmap, probes}; preview {channel}. Mesh processing: boolean {op?, with?, out?} (no with = union all shells), remesh {method:voxel|quad|cleanup}, decimate {ratio|triangles|max_error}, cluster_lod (glb + .clod), visibility. Ships+structures: hull {plan,profile,sections,panel_lines,plates}, assemblies (canopy engine wing landing_gear ramp turret corridor door engine_room tank crane market_stall ...), on_hull, neon, light, fog_card; template:gunship (hero, walkable)|fighter|dropship|hauler|capital_ring; kit; livery; generate {kind:interior|mining_colony|market}; budget; preview mood; export static|split|budget|walk; walk_check (player metrics). Damage: damage {states:[scuffed|damaged|wrecked|{name,amount,regions}], kind?:door|terminal|crate|barrel|glass|light|hull|engine} = variants + fx sockets; fracture {groups:[{part,pieces,debris?,close?}]} (open parts are closed first; close:false refuses); preview|render {damage:<state>}; export adds <name>.damage.glb + masks (damage:{mode,vertex,lods,profile:"roblox"}; rigs and skins kept per state and LOD, skinned chunks on bones; lods / bake_ao keep rigs and skins). New models get one cohesive UV atlas canvas <name>_uv (world-aligned bake + contact AO + edge wear; paint it; unwrap:false = per-part); unwrap {name, unwrap?:{do,texel,max_size,cohesion}} redoes / converts it (do:"check" = cohesion report). art_help {topic:"3d"|"damage"}.

Parameters:
- action (string, required): one of create | update | info | list | delete | preview | export | ctm | pose | animate | render | check | trim | skeleton | skin | weights | material | boolean | remesh | decimate | cluster_lod | visibility | kit | livery | generate | budget | walk_check | damage | fracture | unwrap
- name (string)
- weapon (object|boolean)
- arms (object)
- hold (object): {weapon|arms, carry?, attach?, clip?, both?, fix?}
- carries (array of string)
- parts (array of object|object)
- add (array of object)
- set (object)
- remove (array of integer|string)
- template (string): one of fp_arms | fp_rifle | fp_pistol | gunship | fighter | dropship | hauler | capital_ring | melee_combat_knife | melee_machete | melee_baton | melee_stun_baton | melee_vibro_blade | melee_breach_axe | melee_breach_hammer | melee_riot_shield
- textures (object|string)
- rig (object)
- sockets (object)
- poses (object)
- clips (object|array): create / update: {<clip>: {keys, loop?, duration?}}; hold_check: clip names
- pose (string)
- base (string)
- clip (string)
- keys (array|null)
- loop (boolean)
- events (array)
- duration (number)
- ease (enum): one of linear | smooth | step
- delete (boolean)
- canvas (string)
- animation (string)
- frames (integer)
- fps (number)
- view (string|object)
- camera (string|object)
- fov (number)
- zoom (number)
- angles (array)
- sweep (object)
- pivot (array)
- light (object)
- outline (string|boolean)
- quantize (boolean|object)
- only (array of string)
- hide (array of string)
- grid (number)
- scale (number): px per unit (32)
- origin (string|array): auto (part coords)|bottom (props, ships)|center|pivot|[x,y,z]
- notes (string)
- overwrite (boolean)
- overlays (array of object)
- uv_origin (array of number)
- views (array of string|object): game front back side left top iso fp
- size (integer|array): preview px | render [w, h]
- preview (boolean)
- path (string)
- instances (boolean)
- atlas (boolean)
- up (string): one of y | z
- normal_maps (boolean)
- ctm (object): base|template|overlay, method, border{width,style,color}, connect, from, weights, tile
- bake_ao (boolean|object)
- bump (number|object)
- lods (array of number)
- lod_mode (enum): one of nodes | files
- lod_screen (object)
- impostor (boolean|object)
- collision (boolean|string|object)
- occluder (boolean|string|object)

Hand-drawn, no 3D: template {kind:gun|mag|attachment|item|arm, name, class?, view?:hip|ads|reload|side|rear|top (or yaw, pitch, roll), part?:upper|fore|hand, pose?, side?} = canvas with guides; anchors {canvas, set?, remove?, suggest?, accept?} (+ checks); sweep2d {out, sources?}; trace {skin, name, parts?, poses?, views?} = 3D arms -> editable 2D skin. ## 3. Draw commands (art_draw ops)

Each is {"op":"<name>", ...fields} inside art_draw commands. Same text as art_help {topic:"ops"}.

grid {x?,y?,rows:[str],legend?,cpp?} — paint from text rows (1 char = 1 px; "." keeps). Each char is a palette key or a legend entry. "." and " " leave pixels unchanged; legend {"_":"transparent"} erases. cpp:2 = two chars per pixel for multi-char palette keys ("s1"). Best tool for deliberate hand-placed detail (faces, icons, outlines).
example: {"op":"grid","x":4,"y":2,"legend":{"o":"#2a1a22","s":"#e8b090"},"rows":[".oo.","osso","osso",".oo."]}

pixels {points:[[x,y,color?]],color?} — single pixels. points may carry their own color: [x,y,"#f00"].
example: {"op":"pixels","color":"#fff","points":[[3,3],[4,3,"#ff0"]]}

line {x1,y1,x2,y2|points,color,width?,pixel_perfect?} — line/polyline. brush: round|square. pixel_perfect:true removes L-shaped doubles (clean 1px lines). points:[[x,y],...] draws a polyline.
example: {"op":"line","x1":0,"y1":15,"x2":15,"y2":0,"color":"o","pixel_perfect":true}

curve {points:[3|4 pts],color,width?} — bezier. 3 points = quadratic, 4 = cubic bezier. Pixel-perfect. Use for hair, tails, round outlines.
example: {"op":"curve","points":[[2,12],[8,0],[14,12]],"color":"o"}

polygon {points,color?,outline?,fill?} — polygon. fill defaults to true; outline = border color.
example: {"op":"polygon","points":[[8,1],[15,14],[1,14]],"color":"g2","outline":"o"}

rect {x,y,w,h,color?,outline?,fill?,thickness?} — rectangle. fill:false with color draws only the border.
example: {"op":"rect","x":2,"y":2,"w":12,"h":8,"color":"w2","outline":"o"}

ellipse {x,y,w,h,color?,outline?,fill?,thickness?} — ellipse in a box. Bounding box x,y,w,h. fill:false with color draws only the border; thickness = border width in px (like rect).
example: {"op":"ellipse","x":2,"y":2,"w":12,"h":12,"color":"r2","outline":"o"}

fill {x,y,color,tolerance?,contiguous?} — flood fill. Flood fill on the target layer; contiguous:false replaces the color everywhere; diagonal:true spreads through corners.
example: {"op":"fill","x":8,"y":8,"color":"b2"}

text {x,y,text,color,font?,scale?,align?,shadow?} — pixel font. Built-in pixel fonts, uppercase (A-Z 0-9 punctuation, \n). font "3x5" (default, tiny), "5x7" (readable UI/labels) or "7x9" (titles). scale multiplies; align left|center|right around x; spacing, line_spacing in px.
example: {"op":"text","x":32,"y":4,"text":"HELLO","color":"#fff","align":"center","shadow":"#000"}

replace {from,to,tolerance?,region} — swap one color. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"replace","from":"#ff0000","to":"r2"}

remap {map:{from:to},tolerance?,region} — swap several colors (variants). Swap several colors at once (derive color variants of an asset). Errors listing the colors present if nothing matched (allow_none:true to skip). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"remap","map":{"r1":"b1","r2":"b2","r3":"b3"}}

gradient {colors,direction?,dither?,region} — banded gradient. direction: vertical|horizontal|diagonal|diagonal-reverse|radial. dither: bayer (default)|noise|none (false = none). Banded to the given colors. radial reaches the last color on the region edge (corners filled with it). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"gradient","colors":["#1a1030","#4a2a60","#c06070"],"direction":"vertical"}

adjust {hue?,saturation?,lightness?,jitter?,alpha?,region} — HSL adjust. hue in degrees, saturation/lightness -1..1, jitter = random ±lightness per pixel, alpha = opacity change -1..1 (-0.3 = 30% more transparent; result clamped 0..1), set_alpha = absolute opacity 0..1. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"adjust","lightness":-0.1,"hue":10}

quantize {colors?,dither?,alpha_threshold?,region} — snap to palette. Snap pixels to colors (default: the palette; colors:16 = best 16 from the region). dither none|bayer, strength. alpha_threshold:0.5 makes alpha binary. Run after effects to keep a coherent palette. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"quantize","dither":"bayer"}

shade {colors:[dark..light],light?,of?,depth?,profile?,per_color?,region} — AUTO form shading of drawn shapes (use instead of hand shading). Shades shapes you already drew (any flat color) from ONE light direction using a ramp dark->light: rounded volume from the shape outline, no pillow shading. of: which colors form the shape (default every painted pixel in the region). light: top-left (default)|top|top-right|left|right|bottom-left|bottom|bottom-right or degrees. profile: round (dome, default)|flat (bevelled edges + flat top, set depth px)|sharp. per_color:true shades each flat color as its own part (e.g. arm vs body). bias -0.3..0.3 shifts lighter/darker; contrast; dither:true; wrap:true for tileable textures; cleanup:0 keeps lone pixels. Workflow: block in flat silhouettes -> shade -> outline -> hand detail. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"shade","colors":["r0","r1","r2","r3","r4"],"of":"r2","light":"top-left"}

cells {colors:[dark..light],gap_color?,size?,gap?,layout?,stretch?,seed?,region} — tileable shaded stones/scales/cracks. Fills the region with a tileable pattern of separately shaded cells: cobblestone (size 5, gap 1), scales (layout brick), bricks (layout brick, stretch 2, profile flat, depth 1), cracked earth (gap_color dark, size 8), gravel (size 3). variation = per-cell tone shift (steps), jitter 0..1, depth/profile/light like shade (light: top-left (default)|top|top-right|left|right|bottom-left|bottom|bottom-right or degrees; profile: round (default)|flat (bevelled, set depth px)|sharp). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"cells","colors":["s0","s1","s2","s3"],"gap_color":"#2e2c36","size":5,"seed":3}

noise {colors,weights?,scale?,octaves?,despeckle?,seed?,region} — tileable noise. Tileable value noise. weights = exact share of each color. scale = feature size px (1 = per-pixel). despeckle:1-2 absorbs lone pixels (flat cartoon surfaces). Prefer cells/shade for stone; noise is for subtle variation. "keep" in colors leaves those pixels unchanged (sparse noise). Under a mask, transparent colors do not erase (no holes in the masked art) unless erase:true. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"noise","colors":["d1","d2","d3"],"weights":[0.3,0.5,0.2],"scale":3,"despeckle":1}

scatter {colors|color,density?|count,size?,seed?,region} — random specks. Random specks/blobs of size px. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"scatter","colors":["g3","g4"],"density":0.05,"size":1,"seed":2}

damage {amount?,seed?,kinds?,on?,palette?,mirror?,region} — cracks/scorch/dents/holes/scratches from the palette. Damage overlay on existing pixel art (armour plates, helmets, sprite props): amount 0..1 (scuffed 0.25, damaged 0.6, wrecked 1), kinds subset of scratches|chips|dents|holes|cracks|under|scorch (default by amount: scratches + chipped edges from 0, dents 0.15, holes 0.2, cracks 0.3, under = bare-metal / primer patches with a dark rim 0.45, scorch 0.5; feature size scales with the damaged box, so a 128x192 prop reads at every amount), on:[colors] = only those pixels (the plates), palette:[colors] (default: the colours already in the region; nothing outside it is ever written). Features sit at the same relative spot of the damaged area's box for the same seed: run it on every frame / view of a rig with one seed (mirror:true on mirrored views). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"damage","amount":0.6,"seed":4,"on":["#5a6878","#7a8898","#3c4652"]}

outline {color,mode?,of?,from_layer?,diagonal?,region} — outline shapes. mode outer (around shapes, default)|inner (on the shape edge). of: only shapes of these colors (selective outline). from_layer: outline another layer's shapes onto this layer. diagonal:true = 8-connected. skip_existing:true = pixels already in the outline color count as outline, not shape, so re-running never doubles it to 2 px (only fills gaps); it is the default when the layer already has that exact color (pass skip_existing:false for a second ring). Region limits where it writes; honours mask. Use a dark hue-shifted color, not pure black.
example: {"op":"outline","color":"#2a1a22"}

bevel {light?,dark?,size?,region} — block edge highlight/shadow. Light top/left and dark bottom/right edge lines of size px (blocks, planks, buttons). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"bevel","light":"w3","dark":"w0"}

copy {x,y,w,h,to_x,to_y,from_canvas?,from_layer?,from_frame?,scale?,flip_x?,tint?,opacity?} — copy/stamp (also across canvases/frames). Copy a block (from this layer, from_layer, from_frame or from_canvas = asset stamp). Order: scale/flip, then hue/saturation/lightness, then tint (multiply), then opacity. skip_transparent defaults true. Build animation frames from a base frame: copy from_frame then move parts.
example: {"op":"copy","from_frame":0,"x":0,"y":0,"w":32,"h":32,"to_x":0,"to_y":1}

flip {axis,region} — flip. axis x|y. region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"flip","axis":"x"}

rotate {turns|angle,expand?,region} — rotate (90° steps or any angle). turns:1..3 = 90° steps (square region). angle:<deg> = any angle with pixel-art-safe rotsprite-style sampling (no new colors). Region defaults to the whole canvas; pivot cx,cy defaults to its centre. Without expand, pixels rotated past the region/frame edge are cut. expand:true = nothing is cut: the canvas (every frame) grows just enough to hold the rotated content (content shifts by the left/top growth) and the result may extend past the region.
example: {"op":"rotate","angle":30,"x":8,"y":8,"w":16,"h":16}

shift {dx,dy,wrap?,region} — move pixels (wrap = fix seams). Move pixels by dx,dy (wrap:true default wraps around: shift by half the size to see/fix tile seams in the middle). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"shift","dx":8,"dy":8}

mirror {axis,source} — mirror half. Copy one half onto the other mirrored: axis x|y, source left|right|top|bottom. Symmetric sprites: draw the left half, mirror.
example: {"op":"mirror","axis":"x","source":"left"}

clear {region?} — erase. No region = the whole layer (with frame: the whole frame). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame). Honours mask.
example: {"op":"clear","x":0,"y":0,"w":4,"h":4}

light {x,y,radius,color,intensity?,mode?,steps?} — point light. mode add|screen|multiply|paint; falloff smooth|linear|sharp; radius_y for ellipses; steps bands (0 = smooth). Paints empty pixels too (on_empty:false = only painted ones). Put lights on their own layer with blend screen/add. region:[x,y,w,h] clips it.
example: {"op":"light","x":40,"y":30,"radius":18,"color":"#ffb060","intensity":0.8,"mode":"add"}

fog {color,from?,to?,direction?,noise?,steps?,region} — haze. direction vertical|up|horizontal|radial; from/to = alpha; noise 0..1 wisps. For big smooth fog use steps:0 then quantize dither bayer once (a few steps + bayer looks like a screen door). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"fog","color":"#8fa6c0","from":0,"to":0.4,"direction":"up","noise":0.4}

rays {x,y,angle,spread,count,width,color,alpha?} — god rays. God rays from x,y: angle (deg, 90 = down), spread, count, width (deg), length, alpha. Draw on a layer with blend screen/add.
example: {"op":"rays","x":20,"y":-10,"angle":60,"spread":30,"count":4,"width":6,"color":"#ffe7a8","alpha":0.4}

glow {threshold?,radius?,intensity?,gain?,normalize?,wrap?} — bloom. Bloom around pixels brighter than threshold. select: value (default, HSV max channel: saturated neon blooms too) | luma (perceived brightness, the previous default) | saturation. Tiny 1-2 px emitters need gain:3-6 or normalize:true. wrap:true for tiling textures. steps bands it.
example: {"op":"glow","threshold":0.7,"radius":2,"gain":3}

blur {radius,region} — blur. Depth of field for far/near layers (passes:1 for lighter). region = x?,y?,w?,h? (defaults to the whole canvas/frame).
example: {"op":"blur","radius":1}

vignette {strength?,radius?,color?} — darken edges. strength 0..1, radius 0..1 where darkening starts.
example: {"op":"vignette","strength":0.5}

cast_shadow {from_layer,dx,dy,color,squash?,skew?,soft?} — drop shadow from a layer. Projects from_layer's shapes onto this layer: dx,dy offset, squash (0.3-0.6 = on the ground), skew, base_y (ground row, default lowest painted row), soft = blur px (banded).
example: {"op":"cast_shadow","from_layer":"hero","dx":3,"dy":0,"squash":0.4,"color":"#00000066","soft":1}

iso_box {at:[gx,gy,gz]|x,y,tile,origin,w|size_left/right,height,top,left?,right?,outline?,edge?,anchor?,inset?} — iso block. 2:1 pixel iso. Position with at:[gx,gy,gz] + tile + origin:[ox,oy] (origin = top vertex of cell 0,0; gx, gy in cells, gz = lift in screen px, so stack a box on one of height 16 with gz:16) or x,y bbox. w = tile width (multiple of 4) or size_left/size_right; tiles_x/tiles_y; height px. Faces auto-shade from top; outline/edge colors. anchor:"center" centres a smaller box on its cell; inset shrinks it; fractional at allowed. Draw back to front (increasing gx+gy). Texture faces afterwards with mask:<face color>.
example: {"op":"iso_box","at":[1,1,0],"tile":32,"origin":[64,20],"height":16,"top":"#b89a72","outline":"#3a2a20"}

iso_tile {same as iso_box without height,color} — iso floor diamond. Flat iso diamond with the iso_box positioning; inset:1 leaves grout gaps.
example: {"op":"iso_tile","at":[0,0,0],"tile":32,"origin":[64,20],"color":"#6a7a5a","inset":1}

## 4. Help topics

art_help {topic:"<name>"} returns each of these. Topics: workflow, textures, characters, animation, scenes, hires, minecraft, rig, library, skin2d, melee, 3d, materials, damage, audio, music, mixing, perception, planets, fx, fp, graph, cleanup.

### Topic: workflow

GOOD PIXEL ART, STEP BY STEP
1. Palette first: art_palette ramp per material (4-5 shades, hue-shifted: cool shadows, warm highlights). Few colors total.
2. Block in flat silhouettes (rect/ellipse/polygon/grid) in one mid color per part.
3. Form: shade {colors:[ramp], of:<part color>} per part (or per_color:true) — one light direction (top-left).
4. Outline: outline {color:<dark hue-shifted>} (outer). Optionally inner lines with grid.
5. Detail by hand (grid rows): eyes, highlights, texture marks. 1px details only where they read.
6. Check: art_critique (numbers + coordinates), then art_view. Fix, repeat. Finish with quantize if effects were used.
Avoid: pillow shading (light on every edge), noise/speckle everywhere, pure black outlines, too many colors, isolated stray pixels.
Paths (every export / import / out / path arg): absolute (C:/x/y.png, forward slashes are fine on Windows) | "./x" = the server's working directory | bare relative = the workspace exports folder (the reply gives the full path). A path ending in an extension is a file; otherwise it is a folder or file stem (the tool's reply lists what it wrote).

### Topic: textures

TILEABLE TEXTURES (blocks, floors, walls)
- Stone/cobble/scales/bricks/gravel: cells (one command) with a 3-5 shade ramp + gap_color; then a few hand details.
- Organic (dirt, sand, grass top): base fill, noise scale 2-4 despeckle:1 with 3 shades, scatter a few highlight specks.
- Wood planks: rect bands, bevel per plank, line grain, a knot with ellipse.
- Metal/gems: rect/polygon facets in a flat color, shade profile:flat depth 2-3, bright 1px highlight, outline.
- Always: art_view tile:3 or art_critique (tiling_seam). Fix seams: shift dx,dy = half size (wrap), repair the middle cross, shift back.
- Variants (colors/dyes): duplicate canvas + remap the ramp.

### Topic: characters

CHARACTERS & SPRITES
- Pick a frame size and keep it (16, 24, 32, 48). Ground line = same row in every frame; leave 1px margin.
- Proportions are a style choice (chibi big head, heroic, realistic, monstrous); keep them identical between frames. Readable silhouette, 1px dark outline.
- Draw on layers per part (body, head, arms, gear) so parts can be shaded (shade per_color) and moved per frame.
- Directions/turnarounds + animations stay consistent with art_rig (parts + poses → generated frames). See art_help topic:"rig".
- Without a rig: draw frame 0, then copy from_frame 0 into the next frame and only move/redraw the parts that change.
- Check animation with art_critique (volume_drift, ground_line, palette_drift) and art_animation filmstrip.

### Topic: animation

ANIMATION
- A canvas with frames = vertical strip of equal frames. art_animation: insert/duplicate/move/delete frames; tag {name, from,to, duration|durations|fps, loop, direction}.
- Key poses first, then in-betweens. Walk: contact, down, passing, up (x2 for left/right). Idle: 2-4 frames, 1px breathing bob. Attack: anticipation, smear, impact, recovery.
- High frame rates (12-24 fps): use art_rig — poses on keyframes, tween generates the in-betweens with sub-pixel-safe rotation.
- Draw a frame: art_draw {frame:N}. Check: art_view {frame, onion:1}, art_animation filmstrip, art_critique.
- Export: art_animation export format gif (preview) | spritesheet (png + Aseprite-style json) | frames. path "out/knight" writes out/knight.png+.json (json:false = png only); a folder path ("out/knight/") writes out/knight/<canvas>.*.

### Topic: scenes

2.5D / HD-2D SCENES
Layers back to front: sky, far, mid, play, foreground. Far = lower contrast, bluer; optional blur. Lights on their own layers (art_layer add blend:"screen"/"add"), shadows blend "multiply", color grade "overlay". fog between depth layers, rays from windows/canopies, glow on emissive pixels. Finish: art_layer stamp_visible + quantize the stamp. Stamp repeated props with copy from_canvas (scaled/tinted for distance). Iso: iso_box/iso_tile back to front. art_canvas normal_map for engine lighting.

### Topic: hires

HIGH-RESOLUTION PIXEL ART (128px .. 2048px)
- Work in regions: art_view x,y,w,h zooms (a big canvas view is downsampled overview), art_read only small regions.
- Block in with shapes + shade (geometry based, resolution independent), cells/noise for surfaces, then detail per region.
- Upscale a small sketch: art_canvas scale {factor, method:"scale2x"} keeps clean pixel edges, then refine.
- Use layers per depth/part; effects (light/fog/glow) scale well.

### Topic: minecraft

MINECRAFT RESOURCE PACKS
Blocks/items 16x16 (Java). Names differ by version: 1.12 textures/blocks + textures/items (planks_oak), 1.13+ block/ + item/ (oak_planks). art_minecraft vanilla lists real names/sizes (references only, never ship vanilla art). Set canvas meta.texture (e.g. "blocks/stone"); art_minecraft build {project} writes the pack + zip. Animated textures = frames. Grass/leaves are grayscale + biome tint (meta.tint for previews).

### Topic: rig

RIGS: CONSISTENT MULTI-VIEW, MULTI-ANIMATION ASSETS (art_rig)
Coordinates: root = where the root part's pivot sits in the frame; a child's "at" = offset of its pivot from the PARENT'S PIVOT (not its corner), so a head on a body with pivot at the body's bottom needs at:[0,-bodyHeight].
A rig = parts (drawn ONCE per view on the "<name>_parts" canvas), joints (pivot + parent + rest offset "at"), and poses (per-part x,y offsets px, rot degrees, sx/sy scale for squash & stretch, variant, hide). Every generated frame is assembled from the same part pixels, so the character stays identical across directions and animations, and in-betweens are tweened at any fps.
0. Quick start: create {name, frame:[32,32], template:"humanoid"|"blob"|"flyer"} gives parts, views, poses and presets (humanoid: idle, blink, walk, run, attack, hurt, jump, death; blob: idle, hop, blink, hurt, death; flyer: fly, hurt, death). Templates are only starting points: in the same create pass parts:{head:{w:14,h:10}, tail:{w,h,pivot,parent:"body",at,z}, arm_b:null}, views, root, poses or presets to change anything; later art_rig update / pose. Then draw the cells and animate {preset:"walk", view:"side"} (any preset field can be overridden, e.g. frames:16, fps:20).
1. Custom: create {name, frame:[w,h], views:["side","front","back"], mirror:{side_left:"side"}, root:[x,y] (where the root part's pivot sits in a frame), parts:{body:{w,h,pivot:[x,y]}, head:{w,h,pivot,parent:"body",at:[dx,dy],z}, arm_f:{..., views:{front:{at:[..],z}, back:{hidden:true}}}, eyes:{..., variants:["closed"]}}}. The reply lists every cell [x,y,w,h] per view; the visible "cells" guide layer marks cells (blue) and pivots (red) and never reaches frames.
2. Draw each part in its cell (flat colors -> shade -> outline), same palette keys in every view. Pivot = the joint (top of a limb, bottom of the neck).
3. pose {pose:"contact", parts:{leg_f:{rot:-30}, leg_b:{rot:30}, arm_f:{rot:25}}} — offsets from the rest pose; from:"<pose>" copies one as a base. Poses work in every view.
4. animate {animation:"walk_side", view:"side", keys:[{pose:"contact"},{pose:"pass"},{pose:"contact",mirror_pairs:true},{pose:"pass"}], frames:12, fps:12, plant_feet:true} -> frames + tag on canvas <name> (or canvas). mirror_pairs swaps *_f/*_b, *_l/*_r parts (second half of a walk). keys may set t (0..1) and ease (smooth|linear|step).
4b. One canvas holds everything: every animate call (default canvas = rig name) appends its frames under its own tag. Preset tags are always <preset>_<view> (walk_side, walk_front, idle_side, ...); animation:<name> picks your own. turnaround {pose?, views?} = one frame per view (tags = view names) for a still front/side/back sheet.
4c. Game-engine extras: every animate saves per-frame anchors (each part's pivot x,y,rot) and spritesheet json frames[].anchors carries them (attach weapons, hats, backpacks, particles). Paper-doll layers: animate the same keys with hide:["head"] (body layer) and only:["head"] (head layer) into different canvases: identical timing and ground shift, so they stack exactly and the head can be swapped in-engine.
5. preview {pose} shows all views side by side with the ground line; art_critique {canvas, animation} checks drift. update {parts:{...}, presets:{...}} resizes/adds parts (keeps drawn pixels) and saves reusable animations.
HIGH-DETAIL CHARACTERS (late-90s pre-rendered / "Replaced" look, 64x96 .. 160x240 frames):
6. create {name, frame:[128,192], template:"humanoid_hd"}: pelvis (root), torso, chest, neck, head(+blink), upper_arm/forearm/hand _f/_b, thigh/shin/foot _f/_b, plus optional slots weapon (child of hand_f), gear_back, gear_hip, cape. Views side, front_side (3/4), front, back_side (3/4), back + mirrors side_left, front_side_left, back_side_left = 8 directions. Presets: idle 12f, blink, walk 16f, run 12f, crouch_walk 16f, aim 1f, shoot 6f, reload 24f, hurt 8f, death 20f, throw 12f (IK, foot planting, cape follow-through on). Elbows/knees bend because limbs are parent chains. Leave unused slots empty or remove them with null.
7. Per-view poses: a pose may hold views:{front:{thigh_f:{rot:0, sy:0.8}}} merged over the base pose in that view (mirror views use their source view); tweening blends them. pose {pose, parts, views}. Side-view rotations splay sideways in front/back: override them there (humanoid_hd presets already do: forward swings become sy foreshortening).
8. IK (two-bone, solved per frame after FK, in each view): pose or key ik:{hand_b:{target:{part:"weapon", at:[14,-2]}, bend:-1}, hand_f:{target:[70,60], rot:0}} rotates the end's parent + grandparent so the end pivot reaches the target. target = frame px of the drawn view, or {part, at:[dx,dy]} in that part's rotated frame (a grip, a holster). bend 1 = joint toward +x when the limb hangs (knees in side view), -1 = elbows. rot = world rotation of the end afterwards (keep a gun level). A key without the entry fades back to FK. plane:"depth" bends toward the camera (front/back views, needs scale_children).
9. animate {..., plant:true} (alias ik_feet) pins stance feet: frames whose ankle is within ~2% of the frame height of the rest ground are contact frames; the ankle sits on the ground row and slides at constant speed through each contact (a standing foot stays put), solved with leg IK. plant:["foot_f"] picks parts; rig "feet" sets the default (auto: parts named foot* with a two-bone chain).
10. Secondary motion: rig secondary:{cape:{stiffness:0..1, damping:0..1, gravity?, inertia?}}; animate {secondary:true} (or an inline map) runs a damped angular spring driven by the parent's motion, so capes, scarves, straps and pouches lag and follow through. Loops are simulated until the seam repeats, so loops stay seamless.
11. Rig options: sampling:"rotsprite" (3x3 supersampling of the 8x Scale2x cell + majority colour + hole/stray cleanup: stable limb thickness, only existing colours; humanoid_hd default) | "smooth" (same on the 1x cell) | "nearest8" (old rigs' default). scale_children:true makes a part's sx/sy also move its children's joints (foreshortening, breathing). Frames per canvas are limited to 8192 px of height: at 128x192 that is 42 frames, so give each preset+view its own canvas (canvas:"hero_walk_side").
12. Export: art_animation export {format:"spritesheet", json:false} skips the sidecar json.
13. Equipment sets: give parts variants (chest:["plate"], head:["helmet","helmet_blink"]) and optionally rig variant_sets:{heavy:{chest:"plate", head:"helmet"}}; animate {..., variant:"heavy"} (or ["heavy","medium"]) renders every part with that set: no per-set sheet swapping. A pose variant (blink) combines as <set>_<variant> (helmet_blink) when the part has it.
14. Replies: create / update / info answer with a summary (cells as rows:{view:y} + parts:{part:[x,w,h]}, so a cell = [x, rows[view], w, h]; poses as names; presets as frames/fps). full:true = the complete JSON; fields:["poses"] = just those fields in full. art_info is a summary too (full:true for palette, meta, frame lists).
HELD WEAPONS (weapon handling, opt-in): create {..., template:"humanoid_hd", weapon:{class:"rifle"|"carbine"|"smg"|"shotgun"|"dmr"|"sniper"|"lmg"|"pistol", attachments?:{vgrip:"vertical_grip"|"angled_grip"|"bipod"|"suppressor"|"optic"|"light"}}} (or update {weapon}). Draw the weapon (and att_<name> cells) in the side row only, pointing RIGHT: the solver projects that cell into every view.
- Points (weapon cell px; defaults are fractions of the cell): points:{grip_main:{at:[x,y], angle}, grip_support:{at, angle, slide?}, stock, muzzle, optic, mag}, sockets:{underbarrel, top, muzzle}. An attachment mounts its cell pivot on its socket and may take over grip_support (vertical/angled grip, bipod), muzzle (suppressor) or optic. attach:[names] = the active ones (animate attach:[...] per call).
- Carry states (long guns): aim (stock in the shoulder pocket, cheek weld to the optic line), ready_low, ready_high, hip, sprint, reload (support hand free for the pouch / magazine), slung, one_hand_low, drop, holster (hidden). Pistols: aim (isosceles, optic at eye height), compressed, low, reload, one_hand_low, holster. A pose or key sets carry:"aim"; weapon.poses maps pose names to states (the humanoid_hd presets come mapped: run = sprint, throw = slung, reload = reload, death drops it); weapon.carry = the default; animate carry:"ready_high" overrides every frame; weapon.states:{name:{base:"hip", at:[fwd, down] (arm lengths from the shoulder), angle (deg, + = muzzle down), lateral, lock:["main","support"], fire?}} adds your own.
- Every frame of every pose and clip: the weapon is placed per state in a 3D body proxy, then both hands lock onto their grips with two-bone IK and wrist rotation; a pistol's support hand cups the trigger hand. Reach uses the rig's arm lengths: the shoulders protract a little, the support hand slides back along a rail, then the weapon moves back along its axis; limbs never stretch and elbows bend down / out. The torso, head and legs (and free arms) are capsules the weapon may not enter (weapon.standoff = minimum chest-to-receiver gap): it is pushed forward first, then outward, turning about the stock when shouldered. Muzzle discipline: outside firing states the muzzle points down / forward-low and never at the own body. Front / back views: a barrel pointing at the camera is canted outward with a length floor (weapon.foreshorten:{floor:0.42, cant:16, back_cant:45} | false).
- Draw order: the weapon goes over the torso when held in front of it and under it when behind (depth from the 3D proxy); weapon.layer:{above:[parts], below:[parts], pin:{<view>|all:"front"|"back"|z}} overrides. layers {name, pose|preset+frame, view} lists the stack with the reason for each z; explain {part_a, part_b, ...} says why one is over the other.
- mirror_pairs swaps legs and free arms but keeps held hands (and the weapon) on their side; key mirror_hands:true swaps the hands on purpose (the weapon moves to the other shoulder).
- check {name, clips?, views?, detail?} runs every frame of every preset in all 8 directions: hand-to-grip distance, arm over-extension, inverted elbows, weapon-body penetration, muzzle flags, layering and weapon visibility (back-facing views only need the muzzle to show) -> pass/fail + the failing frames. animate validates the same way: constraints:"refuse" (default: nothing written), "fix" (auto-correct: muzzle down, stronger cant, flipped elbows, draw order), "warn" or "off". Pose IK targets may name weapon points: ik:{hand_b:{target:{weapon:"mag", at:[0,4]}}} (points: stock, grip_main, grip_support, muzzle, optic, mag, charge).
- Aimed at the camera (front views, firing states) the barrel stays short and is canted INWARD (muzzle toward the centre line; foreshorten.aim_floor 0.24, aim_cant 9), drawn over the forearms and the trigger hand and under the support hand (a pistol's slide over both hands), and the head tilts onto the stock (weld_tilt 10). Seen from behind (back view): the gun is yawed OUTWARD in 3D, by the smallest angle that shows the barrel past the silhouette (outward share >= sin(back_cant)), then projected, so its pitch is kept (a level aim is level, ready_low points down). Every yawed back view has one length (foreshorten.back_floor 0.55), so the sheet cells match the frames. The arms follow the 3D arm solution projected (the elbow sits out and below the shoulder where the 3D elbow is; weapon.back_elbow:false turns this off). Arms holding the gun reach in front of the body: their forearms and hands, and upper arms past the torso's centre, are drawn under the whole trunk (chest and its parents; depth.back_occlusion:false turns this off), and the support shoulder protracts toward the centre line. back_side keeps the 2D rule (muzzle angled out by back_cant). The weapon check flags "elbow raised above the shoulder (seen from behind)" and "<part> drawn over the torso from behind while in front of the body". humanoid_hd with a weapon adds a "mag" part (draw it in the side row; it rides in the mag well) and "mag_hand" (art:"mag": the same cell in the support hand); the reload preset is grab -> strip (mag in hand) -> chest pouch -> seat -> charging handle (state reload_charge) with events mag_out, mag_pouch, mag_in, charge, ready.
DEPTH, DRAW ORDER, LINKED CELLS (2D rotated sprites):
- depth:true (rig option; library skeletons default to it): each arm chain hanging from the chest goes over the chest when it is in front of the chest's front surface, under it behind its back surface, authored order in between; decided per frame with hysteresis in clips (no flicker). depth:{rules:[{part:"upper_arm_b", ref:"chest", chain?:true, split?:true, views?}], margin?, thickness?:{chest:[deep, wide]}}. split: a bone crossing the surface is cut into a pivot piece and a tip piece with their own z.
- z keyframes: a key {pose, z:{forearm_b:9}} sets draw order for that key (steps at the tween midpoint); a pose z wins over the depth model.
- zcheck {name, clips?, views?, window?} -> z-flicker (two overlapping parts swap order and swap back within window frames) and depth violations, with each failing frame's order. layers {name, tag | all_frames:true} gives every frame's stack with the rule per part and debug_render {name, tag|preset|animation, frame} a per-part atlas (animation:"<clip>_<view>" = an art_anim library clip on a skin's rig) (the web UI's Layers view uses both). animate stores per-frame draw order (bottom -> top) in meta.order when depth is on (order:true otherwise); spritesheet json frames[].order / frames[].events.
- Linked cells: parts.p.link:{back_side:"side"} or views.<v>.link:{view, flip?} draws another view's cell (no redraw); parts.p.art:"<part>" draws another part's cell (mag_hand); parts.p.hide:true = hidden until a pose sets hide:false. consistency {name, views?, tolerance?} compares the views of every part (empty cells, palette drift, bone length drift, pivot / joints off the drawing, rest silhouette height). derive {name, from:"side", to:["front_side"], parts?, flip?, overwrite?} copies cells as a start to paint over.
- stable:true (animate; batch default) quantizes each part's drawing angle (3 deg steps, hysteresis) so slow limbs do not shimmer; joints stay exact. events:[{t, name}] on animate / presets -> frames (meta.events).

### Topic: library

ANIMATION LIBRARY (art_anim): author motion once per skeleton, render any skin
1. skeleton {name:"hd", template:"humanoid_hd", frame:[128,192], weapon?:{class:"rifle"}, proportions?:{heavy:{width:1.15, spine:1.04}, lean:{width:0.9, legs:1.04}}} saves the rig definition (no art), masks (lower = pelvis + legs, upper, arms, head, all; masks:{} adds yours) and the clip library: the template presets plus walk_aim (walk legs + aim upper body: a layer with mask "upper"), flinch (additive upper-body hit) and walk_hit. depth:true is on by default. from_rig:<rig> or parts:{...} build one from your own rig.
2. clip {skeleton, name, keys:[{pose|parts, t?, ease?, carry?, z?}], frames, fps, loop?, events?:[{t, name}], plant?, secondary?, carry?} | {layers:[{clip:"walk"}, {clip:"aim", mask:"upper", weight?:1}, {clip:"flinch", additive:true}]}: a layer with a mask overrides those parts (blended by weight, IK ends included); an additive layer adds its offset from its first frame (or ref pose). A clip without keys starts from its first layer. delete:true removes it. from_rig + preset copies a rig preset.
3. skin {name:"mec", skeleton:"hd", proportions?:"heavy" | {...}, parts?, variant_sets?, equipment?:{helmet:{variant:"helmet"}, pack:{part:"gear_back"}}, loadouts?:{light:{equip:["helmet"]}, heavy:{set:"heavy", equip:["helmet","pack"]}}} creates the rig "mec" with the proportioned cells (draw them) or binds an existing rig (rig:<name>, map:{skeleton_part: rig_part}). Clips retarget to the skin's proportions automatically. overwrite:true on an existing skin rebuilds its rig from the skeleton's current parts (e.g. the shield melee added) and keeps the drawn cells; delete:true removes the skin (its rig stays).
4. render {skin, clip, view, loadout?} -> a canvas like art_rig animate. retarget {clip, from, to, map?} copies a clip to another skeleton (named poses inlined, translations scaled by hip height, IK targets moved with the root; rotations unchanged).
5. batch {skins:["mec","sev"], clips?:[...] (default all), views?:"drawn"|"all"|[...], loadouts?:"all"|[...], out:"<assets dir>", manifest?:"manifest/characters.json", pad?:"auto" | n | [l,t,r,b], front?:"auto" | [parts], stable?:true, max_width?} writes characters/<set>/<clip>_<view>.png horizontal strips (+ <clip>_<view>__front.png: parts drawn over the weapon, or the near arm) and merges sprites.<set> = {frame, anchor (ground point), pad, skeleton, skin, loadout, class, anims:{<clip>_<view>: {file, front?, frames, fps, loop, events?, order?: [{frame, parts (bottom -> top)}] where it changes, grid? (wrapped at max_width)}}} into the manifest. pad:"auto" (default) grows the set's frame symmetrically to fit every frame (a rifle barrel in the side view) and records it: the engine anchors on "anchor".
RUNTIME WEAPON LAYERS (game draws the gun; contract: weapons_world + per-frame sockets):
- Handling classes: pistol (pistol, handgun, revolver), smg, rifle (rifle, carbine, energy, dmr, shotgun), lmg, sniper, launcher, none. Every gun of a class keeps grip_support and stock at the class offsets from grip_main (only the barrel / receiver length varies), so hands baked once land on every gun of the class. Tolerance (px at the character frame): support grip [max(2uw, 6% of the class cell), 1.5u] along / across, stock [2uw, 1.5u], foregrip attachments [3uw, 2u] (u = (H-4)/98, uw = min(u, W/66)).
- weapon {name:"ar", class:"dmr", skin:"mec" | frame:[w,h], attachments?:{scope:"optic"}} = a standalone gun asset: rig "weapon_ar" (one side cell pointing RIGHT, grip_main on the pivot, attachment and magazine cells) + library/weapons/ar.json (class, handling, points, sockets). {name, from_skin:"mec"} copies a character's drawn gun. {name, points:{grip_support:[x,y]}} moves points.
- conform {weapon, fix?} checks grip_support / stock (and foregrip attachments) against the class geometry; fix:true moves the points to it.
- weapon_sheet {weapon, out, views?:[front, front_side, side, back_side, back], pitch?:[-45..45 step 15], attach?, skin?} writes weapons_world/<name>.png (rows = views, columns = pitch, grip pixel fixed in every cell) without the magazine, weapons_world/<name>_mag.png (the magazine alone; the engine draws it over the gun unless the socket says mag:false) and weapons_world/<name>_att_<a>.png overlays (same grid), every sheet <= 1024 px (fewer pitch steps when a long gun would not fit; the reply says), and merges weapons_world.<name> = {class, views, pitch, file, frame, grip[], muzzle[], mag, attach} into manifest/weapons_world.json.
- batch {..., weapon:"runtime", pitch?} exports the characters gun-free: the body strip without weapon / attachments / magazine, the __front strip (what is drawn over the gun: support hand, near arm) and per anim class + weapon:[{x, y, rot, pitch, order:"between"|"behind", hidden?, mag?:false}] per frame in the set's frame px (pad, frame and anchor kept). rot = degrees clockwise about the grip on top of the cell for the nearest pitch, pitch = elevation (up +). Mirrored views export mirrored sockets (x about the anchor, rot negated); the engine mirrors drawn views itself. Use the same pitch steps in batch and weapon_sheet.
- composite {skin, weapon, clip, view, select?:[frames]} renders baked vs runtime (body + gun cell at the socket + __front, as the engine draws it) side by side, with the support-grip error per frame.
- weapon_check {skin, class? | weapons?:[...], clips?, views?} = every gun of the class conforms and, drawn at the skin's sockets, puts its support grip under the baked support hand in every frame (within the class tolerance + 1.5 px).
6. gltf {skin, clips?, path?} exports a skinned cutout mesh (a quad per part from the base-view cells, one joint per part, bind = rest pose) with the clips as animations (scale 0 while a part is hidden; events in extras).
Paths: absolute, "./x" = the MCP server's working directory, bare relative = the workspace exports folder (the reply says where it went).

### Topic: skin2d

2D SKINNING (art_rig skin / weights / shapes / chain / export): bend YOUR drawn sprites on the rig's bones
Cutout rigs hinge rigid pieces; a skin deforms one drawing (an arm, a sleeve, a whole character, a strap) so it bends at the elbow instead.
1. Draw the limb as ONE sprite in its host part's cell (art_rig update {parts:{upper_arm_f:{h:36}}} to make room), or a whole character on a canvas. Joints below the host become bones: bone:true parts (no drawing) or parts you list in absorb (their own cells are no longer drawn in views where the skin has a drawing).
2. skin {name, skin:{arm:{part:"upper_arm_f", absorb:["forearm_f"]}}} | {hero:{canvas:"hero_side", at?:[0,0], bones?:"all"}} (canvas = a frame-sized drawing at the rest pose). Options: bones (influences; default host + absorb, "all" for canvases), method heat (default, diffusion along the mesh, Baran-Popovic) | distance (falloff?) | rigid (blend? px), density low|medium|high | lattice step px, smooth passes, paint:[{bone, region:{box:[x,y,w,h]}|{circle:[cx,cy,r]}|{rows:[a,b]}|{above:y}|{below:y}, soft?, value?, mode:set|add|smooth}] (source image px), weight_canvas:{canvas, bone} (grey = weight) | {canvas, colors:{"#ff0000":"forearm_f"}} (same size as the drawing or the frame), outline auto|false|"#hex", sampling rotsprite (default) | nearest8 | smooth, z, views:{<view>:{canvas?, paint?, off?, ...}} (per-view meshes and weights, shared bones: 8-direction rigs).
   The mesh is a pixel-aligned lattice clipped to the opaque pixels (one quad per pixel component per cell, so a 1px gap between legs cuts it); max 4 influences per vertex, weights sum to 1.
3. weights {name, mesh?, view?, bone?} = check (unweighted, pruned > 4, non-normalised, unused bones) + image: the drawing with its lattice | the bone's heat map (blue 0 .. red 1) or the dominant bone per pixel.
4. Pixel-art-safe: inverse mapping (each output pixel -> its triangle -> the rest point -> the nearest source pixel in a Scale2x 8x copy, 3x3 majority), so no blur and no new colours; triangles that only move copy pixels exactly (the rest pose IS the drawing, pixel for pixel); pinholes / stray pixels are cleaned and newly exposed edges get the outline colour. Deterministic. Folds draw children over parents (bone z).
5. shapes {name, mesh, shapes:{breath:{sculpt:[{region:{circle:[8,10,6], soft:2}, scale:[1.1,1.05]}]}, crease:{variant:"crease", fit?:false, driver:{bone:"forearm_f", from:0, to:-100}}, flex:{canvas:"arm_flexed"}}, view?}: sculpt ops move / scale / rotate (about?) / inflate in a region; a variant drawing of the host cell (or a canvas) fits the silhouette and swaps in at weight >= 0.5; driver = corrective weight from the bone's local angle. Keys / poses set weights: keys:[{pose, shapes:{breath:1}}]; preview {shapes:{crease:1}}.
6. Chains and constraints: ik:{tip:{target, chain:5}} = CCD over 5 ancestors (tails, cables, slings), respecting limits:{part:[min,max]} (local deg). rig constrain:[{type:"aim", part, target, axis?}, {type:"look_at", part:"head", target, chain:["neck","chest"], share?, limit?:75}, {type:"copy_rotation", part, from, space?:local|world, invert?, offset?}] (+ weight); target = [x,y] | {part, at} | "<name>" from a pose / key targets:{<name>:[x,y]}.
   chain {name, part:"sling", bones?:6, axis?, secondary?:true} = cable / strap helper: bone-only segments along the drawn strip (pivot at its start), heat-skinned; pin the end with ik:{sling_6:{target:{part:"weapon", at:[20,2]}, chain:6}}, sway with secondary.
7. Clips: art_rig animate / art_anim render + batch work unchanged (same bone names as humanoid_hd). export {name, presets?, views?, layers?:true, path?} writes <name>.skin2d.json (format agent-art-skin2d v1: bones with bind positions per view, rigid part cells in parts.png, meshes with vertices (bind frame px), uvs (texture px, pages stacked vertically), triangles in draw order, joints + weights (4 per vertex, sum 1), shapes (per-vertex offsets, driver, swap texture), clips baked per frame: bones {name:[x,y,rot,sx,sy]}, shape weights, draw order), strips/<clip>.png and with layers one strip per drawn part / mesh. Runtime: v = sum w_k * M_k * (v_bind + shape offsets - bind_k), M = translate * rotate(deg, y down) * scale; nearest filtering. three.js: BufferGeometry, rewrite position each frame (or a SkinnedMesh with 2D bones); Roblox: EditableMesh SetPosition per vertex, or the layered ImageLabel strips.
Limits: the lattice follows pixel components, not a traced contour; a mesh draws at its host's z (bone z only orders its own triangles); variant sets / equipment do not swap skinned drawings.

### Topic: melee

MELEE (art_anim melee / melee_check / melee_sheet / paired; art_model melee_<weapon>)
Weapons (art_model template:"melee_<id>", cm units, grip at the origin, blade along -Z, edge down): combat_knife, machete, baton (clips extend/collapse), stun_baton (arc_on/arc_off/arc_loop, emissive tip), vibro_blade (unfold/fold/hum), breach_axe, breach_hammer (two-handed), riot_shield (deploy/fold). Sockets on every weapon: grip guard pommel tip edge_a edge_b strike (+ emitter on the stun baton). model render {angles} returns them per frame (meta.anchors, "socket_<name>").
1. melee {skeleton, weapon?:"machete", shield?:true, clips?, overwrite?} on a humanoid_hd skeleton: resizes the weapon cell for the weapon (grip on the pivot, pointing RIGHT, edge on the bottom), adds a "shield" part on forearm_b (cells at body scale: the 92 cm shield is ~half the body height, 24x45 in a 64x96 frame), writes the clip set. Gun skeletons (weapon:{class}) get butt_stroke (rifle) / pistol_whip (pistol) instead. Sets: knife (knife_slash, knife_stab, knife_combo), blade (heavy_swing), baton (baton_strike; shock tip on the stun baton), heavy (two-handed heavy_swing), rifle, pistol, unarmed; shield:true adds shield_bash + shield_up; every set: kick, shove, block, parry, hit_ and stagger_{front,back,left,right}, knockdown, get_up; paired: takedown_rear, disarm_front, shield_knockdown (shield) as <pair>_attacker + <pair>_victim. On gun skeletons disarm_front is a gun disarm for every handling class (long guns and pistols): the victim holds its gun (rifle ready_low / pistol compressed), the attacker (own gun slung / holstered) grabs the gun hand, the victim's hands let go at the transfer and the gun goes to the attacker's main hand (disarm:"take", default) or falls (disarm:"drop"); a body blow follows. melee {skeleton, disarm:"take"|"drop"}.
2. Draw the skin cells as usual (art_anim skin), then melee_check {skeleton|skin, clips?, views?, tolerance?:2}: per clip pass + issues + numbers: no foot or hand drawn below the view's ground row in any view (foot_sink_px, hand_sink_px; melee clips get ground contact: a foot or hand below the ground row is lifted onto it by limb IK, foreshortening in depth in front / back; clip ground:false turns it off); windup -> active_start <= impact <= active_end < recovery for every hit; no active frame before the windup; the weapon edge (or limb) sampled 16x between frames stays inside the exported volumes (sweep_miss_px; the swept hulls are built from 8 sub-steps, so a weapon the handling solver moves abruptly between frames stays covered); paired: planted feet do not slide (foot_slide_px, each actor) or slide against each other (feet_relative_px, until release_frame), no foot or hand of either actor sinks under its ground row in any view, contact points meet in every view (contact_px, contact_by_view; a shield face touching the body counts as 0). Front / back views overlap the partners in depth, so their contacts are measured in 3D: the screen gap of that view + the depth gap (forward axis) from the side view. The side views draw a face-to-face partner from a mirror view (its near hand stays the near hand), so in front / back that partner is staged in depth and drawn mirrored as well (paired.partner_flip: mirror the partner sprite about its root; draw order = paired.order from the 3D depth): its weapon hand stays on the same side as in the side views and the contacts meet in depth. Only what that cannot resolve is staged sideways per frame (lateral_px; the batch manifest's paired.partner_dx_track): <= 3 px at 128x192 for the melee sets. Gun disarm: transfer_frame, transfer_mode, victim_released, transfer_grip_px (take: the taking hand is at the gun), drop_rest_px (drop: the gun lies still at the end), transfer_jump_px (the gun rides the victim's socket smoothly before the transfer). victim_skin:<skin> checks a pair whose victim has other proportions.
PER-SKELETON TAKEDOWNS: skins with proportions (art_anim skeleton proportions + skin proportions) get every paired pair retargeted and refit on their own rigs (the offset of fit / rigid contacts and the hand IK targets are solved again): batch, paired {skin, victim_skin} and melee_check {skin, victim_skin} (refit_offset) all use the refit pair. Heavy on light and light on heavy are both solved: where a foreshortened front-view arm falls short (a light attacker's choke on a much taller victim, a hand crossing the chest) the hand IK reaches in depth (plane:"depth") or swings the arm into the frontal plane (full length), whichever lands closer. The offset fit searches an absolute grid (1/20 body unit) widened until the optimum is inside it, ties take the middle: refits are deterministic and idempotent.
3. batch {skins, clips, views, out} -> anims.<clip>_<view>.melee in the characters manifest (only for clips that have melee data; everything else is unchanged).
4. melee_sheet {weapons?, out, frame?:[64,96], pitch?:[-45..45 step 15], outline?} -> weapons_melee/<id>.png (rows = views front, front_side, side, back_side, back; columns = pitch; the grip on the same pixel in every cell) + manifest/melee_weapons.json melee_world.<id> = {file, frame, grip, views, pitch, px_per_m, set, hands, damage, stamina, radius_px, radius_cm, cells[view][pitch] = {edge:[a,b], tip, strike, angle, length}}.
5. paired {skin, victim_skin?, pair, view?} -> both actors composited at the shared alignment (canvas + contact sheet).
6. FIRST PERSON (art_fp batch, the fp v2 clip / socket format): melee clips get anims.<clip>.melee in manifest/fp.json: gun classes "melee" (long guns jab support -> muzzle, pistols whip), knife slash / stab / combo (3 hits, combo input windows), unarmed melee (punch), and the baton class (baton, stun_baton, club: strike with a shock tip; shield_up = block window, block_arc 140; shield_bash with the riot shield as item2 in the left hand: anims.<clip>.item2 is a per-frame socket like item; fp sweep items baton + riot_shield). Same fields as below (kind, damage, stamina, phase, events, windows, combo, block, push, stagger, shock) in fp frames: events = [{f, e, hit?, damage?, sound?, effect?}] (the fp event format; the clip's own anim.events keep their "hit" key on the impact frame); hits = [{f, hit, volumes:[{source: gun|item|item2|fist, a, b, r (frame px, 384x216), sweep?, eye:{a, b, r} (cm, eye space: x right, y up, -z forward)}]}]. Test the eye capsules in camera space (the camera's world matrix takes them to world) or the px capsule + sweep on screen. art_fp check runs the same order / coverage / sweep checks (melee_clips, worst.melee_sweep_px). The fp riot shield is melee_riot_shield at a 0.55 view-model scale (the full 92 cm panel at arm's length overflows the frame and a 1024 px sweep cell).
MANIFEST anims.<clip>_<view>.melee (frames are strip indices, px are frame px incl. pad, y down):
- set, weapon?, kind (attack | block | parry | reaction), damage (blunt | slash | pierce | shock | null), damage_per_hit? (combo), stamina.
- phase[frame] = idle | windup | active | recovery | block | parry | reaction; windows = [[first, last] active frame per hit].
- events = [{frame, name, hit?, damage?, sound?, effect?, part?}] sorted; names: windup, active_start, impact, active_end, recovery, sfx (sound), vfx (effect), block_start/end, parry_start/end, sync, contact (part), and clip events: disarm, drop_body, down, up, impact (reactions).
- hits = [{frame, hit, volumes:[{source, a:[x,y], b:[x,y], r, sweep?:[[x,y]..], space:{a:[fwd,up,0], b, r}, shock_from?}]}] per active frame: a capsule a-b radius r around the weapon edge / limb; sweep = convex polygon of the edge swept since the previous frame (test it too, or fast hits tunnel); space = the same capsule in body units from the root (side view, + forward / + up; 98 units = 1.8 m) for a 3D or physics test. shock_from = fraction along a-b where the shock tip starts (stun baton: shock = {from, damage:"shock"}).
- root_motion[frame] (body units forward from the clip start; move the entity by it), root_end (paired attacker: move the entity forward this much when the clip ends), block / parry [first, last], block_arc (deg), stagger, knockdown, push, damage_scale, direction, down, lethal, drops_weapon (frame), interrupt ([[first,last]] or {attacker, victim}), combo [{from, to, next_by?}] (input window for the next hit).
- socket[frame] = {x, y, rot, pitch, scale, order: behind|between} | {hidden} for the held melee weapon: draw melee_world.<weapon> cell [view row][nearest pitch] with its grip on (x, y), rotated so the sheet angle matches rot (or as is when you only snap pitch).
- paired = {role, partner, offset:[fwd, lateral] (body units, the partner's root from yours at the clip start, in your facing), facing (deg, 180 = toward each other), sync_frame, release_frame? (from here the victim moves on its own: its fall; alignment no longer holds), partner_view, partner_dx / partner_depth (px in this view), partner_dx_track? (front / back views: partner_dx per frame with the lateral staging; use it instead of partner_dx), partner_flip? (front / back of a face-to-face pair: draw the partner mirrored about its root), order: partner_front|partner_behind, contacts:[{frames, attacker, victim}]}. Both roots stay still during the clip.
- transfer (gun disarm) = {mode: take | drop, frame, track[frame] = {owner: victim | attacker | world, state: held | grabbed | dropped, x, y (the gun's grip_main, frame px of this clip), rot, pitch}}: draw the gun on the owner's weapon layer at (x, y) rotated by rot (the weapon_sheet cell of that pitch); hide the victim's own weapon layer from the transfer frame (take: its weapon solver holsters it; drop: it is the world gun).
THREE.JS RUNTIME: one sprite per actor (strip + manifest frame/anchor). Step at fps; fire events by frame. On active frames transform each volume to world: x_world = entity + facing * (space.a[0] * m_per_unit), y from space.a[1] (m_per_unit = 1.8 / 98), or, for screen-space picking, test the px capsule + sweep in the drawn view. Overlap test: segment-capsule distance <= r + target radius; once per hit index per target. Block: if the defender's phase is block and the attacker is inside block_arc of its facing, cancel damage (parry window: stagger the attacker). Paired: start both on the same tick, place the victim at offset (rotate by the attacker's facing), face it by facing, draw by order, lock input until release_frame, then apply root_end.
ROBLOX: same data as JSON (HttpService:JSONDecode or a ModuleScript). Sprites: SurfaceGui / BillboardGui ImageLabel with ImageRectOffset per frame (strips <= 1024 px wide; split long strips).
