INSTRUMENTS: art_audio {action:"instrument"} lists presets; {name:"metal_guitar"} shows the patch JSON; save a tweak {name:"my_gtr", patch:{base:"metal_guitar", fx:[{gain:40}]}}; audition {name, notes:"E5 _ F5 _"}.
Presets: cathedral_organ choir_pad boys_choir church_bells tubular_bell metal_guitar bass_guitar sub_bass rumble_bass strings_pad low_brass_stab dread_drone heartbeat wind_ambience sampler metal_kit industrial_kit; drums: metal_kick metal_snare metal_tom1 metal_tom2 metal_tom3 metal_hat metal_ohat metal_crash metal_china metal_ride ind_kick ind_snare ind_tom1 ind_tom2 ind_tom3 ind_hat ind_ohat ind_crash ind_ride clap.
Patch = {sources:[{type:osc|additive|modal|fm|pluck|bowed|noise|metal|sample, ...}], amp:{a,d,s,r}, filter:{type,cutoff,q,keytrack,env,env_amount,lfo}, pitch_env, vibrato, mute:{...palm-mute overrides}, layers:[{max_vel, ...velocity layer}], hits, oneshot, fx:[...], gain, pan, width, reverb (send), double (L/R takes), humanize:{time,vel}, round_robin, octave}.
SAMPLES: art_audio {action:"import", path:"kick.wav"} (mp3/ogg via ffmpeg) -> instrument {name:"my_kick", patch:{base:"sampler", sources:[{zones:[{sample:"kick", root:"c3", lo:"c0", hi:"c8", vel:[0,1]}]}]}}.
VOICE ACTING (ElevenLabs): art_audio {action:"voice", name:"guard_halt", text:"Halt! Who goes there?", voice:"<name or voice_id>", model?:"eleven_multilingual_v2", stability?:0.5, similarity?:0.75, style?:0, speed?:1, seed?, language?:"en", previous_text?/next_text? (continuity across lines), sample_rate?:24000 (44100/48000 need an ElevenLabs Pro plan)} -> a sample asset (analyze, critique, export, sampler zones like any import). The same text + voice + settings reuses the saved take (no credits); force:true makes a new one. {action:"voices", search?:"deep"} lists voices. The API key is never a tool argument: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY as a system / user environment variable or in a .env file in the project folder (the server's working directory) or the workspace (a .env is read on each call; a new environment variable needs a server restart).
EXPORT: {action:"export", name:"gib_burst_*", format:"wav|mp3|ogg|opus", bits:16|24|32, bitrate:192, stems:true, layers:true, path:"sfx/"} -> files + <name>.json sidecar (seed + recipe to re-render). Loops get a WAV smpl chunk and OGG LOOPSTART/LOOPLENGTH tags. mp3/ogg/opus need ffmpeg (AGENT_ART_FFMPEG or PATH).
SAMPLE RATE: renders run at 44100 Hz; sample_rate:48000 (on export, or stored on song/sfx/render) delivers 48 kHz through a windowed-sinc resampler. Loop points stay sample-exact (the loop body is resampled as a seamless periodic segment); the sidecar/manifest report the delivered rate, samples and loop.
Topics: music (notation + genre recipes), mixing (chains, buses, mastering), perception (how to read analyze/critique).

### Topic: music

MUSIC NOTATION (art_audio song). JSON {name, tempo, time:"4/4", key:"e phrygian", tracks:{...}, sections:{...}, arrangement:[...], loop} or {name, text:"..."} (same thing as lines).
TEXT + JSON: send both and they deep-merge: the text is parsed first, then every JSON key is merged on top (objects merge key by key, scalars and plain arrays replace, null deletes a key). So {text:"...", tracks:{gtr:{fx:[...], gain:-4}}, buses:{drums:{fx:[{type:"comp",ratio:4}]}}, master:{target_lufs:-16}} keeps the text's notes and instruments and only adds/overrides those fields; tracks.<t>.instrument in JSON replaces the text's instrument for that track.
TRACKS: {gtr:{instrument:"metal_guitar", gain:-6, pan:0, reverb:0.1 (send), octave:2, root_only, transpose, double, humanize:{time:0.006,vel:0.06}, fx:[...appended inserts], bus:"music"|"drums", automation:{gain:[[bar,dB],...], pan, cutoff}}}.
SECTIONS: {verse:{bars:8, <track>: <pattern>, transpose?, vel?}}. Missing track = silent. Patterns repeat to fill the bars.
- Step pattern (drums, one char per 16th): "x...x...x.x.x..." X accent, x hit, o ghost, 1-9 velocity, . rest, | ignored.
- Kit tracks take an object: {kick:"x...x...", snare:"....x...", hat:"x.x.x.x.", ohat, crash, ride, china, tom1-3, clap}.
- Note line: bars split by "|", tokens share their bar evenly: "Em | C" one chord per bar; "e2 e2 f2 e2" quarters; 16 tokens = 16ths.
  lowercase = note (e2 f#3 bb1); Uppercase = chord at the track octave (Em C5 Bdim Am7 Fsus4; X5 = power chord); roman numerals vs key (i iv bVI V7); stacks e2+b2+e3;
  "_" holds the previous note, "." rests, tok*4 repeats. Suffixes: ! accent, ? ghost, ' palm-mute/staccato, ~ legato, % tremolo picking, < swell, @0.6 velocity.
- Generators inline: {gen:"doom_riff", style:"chug|gallop|doom|breakdown|tremolo", seed}, {gen:"organ_progression", style:"dirge|phrygian|liturgical|harmonic"}, {gen:"blast_beat", style:"blast|hammer|gravity|double_kick|dbeat|half_time|doom|four_floor|breakbeat|trap|rock", fill}, {gen:"dread_ambient", part:"drone|bells|heartbeat|wind"}. art_audio {action:"generate", generator, ...} returns the text to edit.
PARTIAL UPDATE: re-send a saved song (same name) with only tracks or only sections: they merge into it per track/section (null removes one); everything else is kept.
ARRANGEMENT: ["intro","verse","verse","chorus"] or "intro verse*2 chorus". loop: true (whole song loops seamlessly: tails wrap to the start) | "verse" (intro plays once) | false. swing: 0..0.5. layers:{explore:["organ","drone"], combat:["gtr","bass","drums"], boss:["choir"]} -> export {layers:true} = one file per intensity layer + manifest.
SCALES: major minor dorian phrygian lydian mixolydian locrian harmonic_minor melodic_minor phrygian_dominant hungarian_minor double_harmonic pentatonic_minor blues diminished.
GENRE RECIPES (compare with critique {genre}):
- hard_techno: 145-165 BPM; a four-on-the-floor kick on every beat, distorted, with a long rumbling tail; an off-beat open hat (on the "and" of each beat); a rumbling sub-bass that pumps with the kick; 150-160 BPM; loud, compressed master (around -7 LUFS)
- techno: 125-140 BPM; four-on-the-floor kick; off-beat hats; a hypnotic, repeating bass/synth loop; 125-140 BPM
- house: 118-128 BPM; four-on-the-floor kick; claps/snares on 2 and 4; off-beat open hats with some swing; a groovy bassline; 118-128 BPM
- drum_and_bass: 165-180 BPM; a syncopated breakbeat (kick on 1 and the "and" of 3, snares on 2 and 4 at half-time feel); a heavy reese or sub bass; 170-176 BPM that feels like 85-88 BPM
- doom_metal: 50-95 BPM; slow, crushing, down-tuned power-chord riffs that ring out; heavy distorted guitars carrying the low-mids; slow half-time drums with big crashes; below ~95 BPM
- death_metal: 150-260 BPM; blast beats and continuous double-kick; fast, tight, palm-muted chromatic riffs; very dense low-mid guitars; 150+ BPM drums
- black_metal: 140-240 BPM; blast beats; tremolo-picked, trebly guitars as a wall of sound; cold, reverberant atmosphere
- industrial: 90-140 BPM; mechanical, metallic, distorted percussion; machine-tight timing; noisy, abrasive textures; distorted bass/synth riffs
- dark_ambient: no clear beat; slowly evolving drones and textures; vast reverb; low, dark spectrum; quiet dynamics (around -18 LUFS)
- gothic_cathedral: 40-110 BPM; pipe organ chords with rich harmonics; choir; cathedral-sized reverb (RT60 over 3 s); minor/modal harmony
- cathedral_doom: 60-140 BPM; heavy distorted power-chord riffs, slow to mid tempo; pipe organ and choir layered over the guitars; cathedral reverb on organ/choir (guitars drier); brutal drums: half-time sections plus double-kick or blast-beat climaxes; minor/phrygian harmony
- orchestral_horror: bowed strings (clusters, tremolo, swells); low brass stabs; big dynamic contrast and silences; dissonance (minor seconds, tritones)
- chiptune: 110-180 BPM; square/pulse and triangle waves; noise-channel drums; arpeggios; almost no reverb; bright, simple timbres
- synthwave: 80-118 BPM; gated-reverb snare on 2 and 4; driving 8th/16th-note analog bass arpeggio; lush detuned pads and lead; big chorus/reverb
- trap: 130-170 BPM; half-time snare/clap on beat 3; rolling 16th/32nd hi-hats with rolls; long 808 sub-bass glides; 130-170 BPM felt at half time
WORKED: gothic cathedral doom (organ intro, doom-riff verse, blast section, choir breakdown, loopable, 76.8 s): art_audio {action:"song", name:"cathedral_doom", intent:"gothic cathedral doom: slow-to-mid heavy riffs, organ and choir, cathedral reverb, brutal drums", genre:"cathedral_doom", text:<below>}
tempo 100
time 4/4
key e phrygian
reverb cathedral
loop all
master target_lufs=-14
track organ cathedral_organ:full gain=-5 reverb=0.6 hp=220 cut=900 cut_db=-6 cut_q=0.7
track pedal cathedral_organ:pedal gain=-3 reverb=0.5 octave=2 root_only=true
track choir choir_pad gain=-5 reverb=0.7
track bells church_bells gain=-3 reverb=0.6 hp=300
track gtr metal_guitar gain=-3 octave=2
track bass bass_guitar gain=-8 octave=1 root_only=true
track drums metal_kit gain=-5
track drone dread_drone gain=-6 reverb=0.4

### Topic: mixing

MIXING + MASTERING
Signal flow: voice -> track inserts (patch.fx + track.fx) -> pan/width/gain/automation -> bus ("drums" for kits, else "music"; song.buses:{drums:{fx:[...], gain}}) -> master. Sends: track.reverb (0..1) into ONE shared song reverb (song.reverb: room|studio|hall|plate|crypt|cathedral|cathedral_huge, or {preset, type:"convolution"} for a generated impulse response, return:dB), track.delay into song.delay {time:"1/8d", feedback}.
Carving shorthands on a track (also in song text): hp=Hz lp=Hz cut=Hz cut_db=-3 cut_q=1.2 boost=Hz boost_db=2, e.g. "track organ cathedral_organ hp=220 cut=900 cut_db=-6". analyze view:"mix" shows which stems mask each other and where.
FX (any numeric param in songs may be an automation curve [[bar, value], ...]; in sfx seconds; every fx takes mix 0..1):
 eq {bands:[{type:peak|lowshelf|highshelf|hp|lp|notch|bp, f, q, gain, poles}]}  filter {ftype, f, q, lfo:{rate,depth}}  drive/saturate {drive dB, shape:tanh|tube|soft|hard|fold|fuzz}
 amp {gain, tight, mid, mid_gain, bass, scoop, treble, presence, level}  cab {lp, hp, res}  bitcrush {bits, rate}  chorus {voices, delay, depth, rate}  flanger  delay {time, feedback, pingpong}
 reverb {preset, wet, conv:true}  comp {threshold, ratio, attack, release, knee, makeup, auto_makeup, key:"<track>"}  duck {from:"kick", amount:6, release:0.18} (sidechain)
 gate {threshold, range, hold}  transient {attack, sustain}  multiband {crossovers:[150,2500], bands:[{threshold,ratio,gain}...]}  limit {ceiling}  formant {vowel, voice, morph:[...], rate}
 tremolo {rate|"1/8", depth}  width {amount}  gain {db}  pan {pan}  fade {in, out}  dc.
MASTER (song.master): {target_lufs:-14 (streaming) | -16..-18 (game music), ceiling:-1 (dBTP), glue:true, glue_threshold, glue_ratio, eq:[bands], bypass}. Chain: HP 25 Hz -> glue comp -> gain to target -> lookahead true-peak-safe limiter. 16-bit export is TPDF-dithered. SFX: peak -1 dBFS.
Metal guitars: 2 takes (double:true) panned L/R, amp gain 30-40, tight 100-130 Hz, cab lp ~5 kHz, cut 300-500 Hz; bass under them, drier; organ/choir HP at 100-200 Hz in dense sections so the guitars keep the low-mids; reverb on organ/choir, little on guitars/kick.
Fixing masking: carve one side (eq peak -3 dB at the overlap), pan apart, or arrange them in different registers. Fixing "buried": +3..6 dB or cut the masker.

### Topic: perception

READING ANALYSIS (you cannot hear: these fields say what a human hears)
analyze {name, view?:"overview"|"mix", intent?, genre?} -> image + stats + report + perception (view:"mix": the stem image + mix fields only); critique {name, intent?, genre?} -> issues ranked by audibility + fixes + report.
IMAGE overview: waveform (L top / R bottom, white lines = bars, ticks = beats), HITS strip (red kick, yellow snare, cyan hats onsets), log spectrogram 30 Hz-16 kHz (guitar body 100 Hz-5 kHz, kick in the sub, organ = stacked horizontal harmonic lines, cymbals = noise above 5 kHz), LUFS (grey momentary, yellow short-term, green dashed target, pink = energy per section), goniometer (vertical line = mono, wide blob = wide), band bars, facts. view:"mix" = each stem's spectrum, red bands = masking, stem balance + masked %.
RHYTHM: perceived_bpm = what a listener taps (tactus), feel says double/half-time vs written; kick_pattern (four_on_the_floor, backbeat, half_time, blast, double_kick, breakbeat, dbeat, trap, sparse, none); patterns = 16-step occupancy (X always, x often, o sometimes); hits_per_bar; swing; timing_spread_ms (<1 ms = machine-tight); syncopation; drive_words. Writing 175 BPM does not make it techno: a four_on_the_floor kick + offbeat hats + rumble bass does.
TONAL: key + mode estimate, progression per bar, distinct chords, tension curve (roughness + loudness).
TIMBRE: brightness; distortion (0..1) + distortion_words come from harmonic structure on pitched, loud frames (energy pushed into upper harmonics / intermodulation, harmonic_extension_db), so reverb wash, drones and drum kits no longer read as distortion; space + reverb_rt60_s (dry < 0.35 s, room, hall, church, cathedral > 3.5 s) measured from free decays (note endings) with reverb_confidence 0..1 (< 0.35 = few free decays, e.g. a dense mix: treat the RT60 as a guess); stereo, organic vs synthetic cues.
SFX (one-shots): reads_as, attack/decay/hits words, pitch_clarity, sweep_octaves (pitch glide while the sound holds its level: a laser/fail falls, a power-up rises; an impact's body drop as it dies away is not a sweep).
GUNSHOTS (recipe or intent names a gun): sfx.transient = attack_ms, snap (share of the first 20 ms above 2 kHz), body, ring_db (strongest spectral peak over the noise), decay30_s. Calibrated on the bundled recordings: real shots ring 5-10 dB and peak within ~1-4 ms; close-mic recordings can be dark (snap 0.02-0.5) and short. critique flags pitched_ring (> 13 dB: sounds like a drum, bell or instrument), soft_attack (> 5 ms, not for distance far), no_crack (a pure tonal thump) and no_tail (a bare click). A score of 100 only means none of these faults were found, not that it sounds right.
KICK/SNARE detection is gated: a kick needs a low-band (35-110 Hz) transient with a sharp, noisy attack and a level near the loudest hits, so sustained choir, wind, organ, drones and sub bass do not read as kicks or backbeats.
MIX (songs): dominant, balance (rel LU, masked %), masking pairs with Hz range, buried, pumping. ENERGY: per-section loudness/density/energy + lift/drop notes. REPETITION: repeated phrases, variety.
GENRE: verdict + gaps vs profiles (hard_techno, techno, house, drum_and_bass, doom_metal, death_metal, black_metal, industrial, dark_ambient, gothic_cathedral, cathedral_doom, orchestral_horror, chiptune, synthwave, trap). INTENT: words from your intent that the audio does or does not support.
REFERENCE: art_audio compare {name, reference:"<asset or file.wav/mp3>"} = spectrum/loudness/dynamics/tempo/groove/stereo differences.
Iterate until critique has no intent_gap/genre_gap and the report describes what you meant.

### Topic: planets

PLANETS AND SPACE (art_planet) — pixel-art planets you see from orbit and land on, terrain, skyboxes
One seeded field per planet (3D noise on the unit sphere) drives every output, so orbit maps, cube faces, mesh LODs,
quadtree tiles and ground patches agree. Textures are palette ramps (banded + ordered dither), NEAREST, max 1024 px.
1. Planet: {"action":"planet","name":"kethra","preset":"bloom","seed":7}
   presets: ice toxic bloom lava desert gas barren. Override anything: radius (mesh units, 100), real_radius_km, relief_km,
   mesh_relief (x4 exaggeration on the mesh), sea_level (0..1 | null), noise {type: fbm|ridged|billow, octaves, frequency, warp},
   continents {frequency, weight}, moisture, biomes:[{name, where:{water?, height?:[a,b], lat?:[a,b], moisture?:[a,b]}, ramp:[dark..light],
   by: height|moisture|lat|noise|depth, rough, emissive?, glow?}] (first match wins, last = fallback), ramps:{<biome>: [...]} (recolour),
   hue (deg), seams {ramp, width, frequency, emissive}, craters {count, min, max, depth}, canyons {amount, width, depth},
   cities {density, color}, clouds {coverage, frequency, color, shadow, levels} | false, rings {inner, outer, ramp, gaps, tilt} | false,
   atmosphere {color, sunset, density, height, falloff} | false, palette:[..] | "project:<name>" (quantise albedo), dither:false.
   Output sizes: equirect (1024 wide), face (256), lods ([48,24,12,6] cells per face edge), tiles {levels:2, segments:16, px:64} | false.
   Files in exports/<name>/: <name>_albedo|height|height16|normal|rough|emissive|night|clouds|rings.png (equirect), cube/<face>_*.png,
   <name>.glb (root with tilt > _lods LOD0..n, _clouds, _atmosphere, _rings), tiles/*.glb + <name>.tiles.json,
   <name>_impostor(_n).png + _disc.png (far LOD), <name>_orbit.png, <name>.planet.json (params, numbers, timings).
2. System: {"action":"system","seed":3,"count":6} -> original star + 4..8 bodies (distinct biomes, orbits, moons),
   <name>.system.json + palette strip render. bake:{equirect:512, face:128} also bakes each body.
3. Ground: {"action":"terrain","planet":"kethra","lat":12,"lon":30,"size":512} -> landing zone (+X east, +Z south, m).
   Relief: planet elevation + detail + ridged-multifractal mountain ranges on some sides of the horizon + dunes (desert) +
   mesas / escarpments, then thermal (scree) + droplet hydraulic (gullies) erosion; a flat pad (pad {radius:40}) stays put.
   Ground: per-biome tilesets painted with cells / noise / scatter / line (plates, ripples, gravel, mud, ice, toxic, moss, snow,
   glow, regolith), 4 variants + 2 transition tiles per layer, 64 px per 2 m (32 px/m); per texel a noise-perturbed splat lookup,
   noise-masked dithered borders with a 1 px rim, strata bands on steep faces. chunks/*.glb (8 px/m, LOD steps [1,2,4,8], skirts,
   collision), detail/*.glb (32 px/m decals around the pad), <name>_horizon.glb (ring to horizon.radius, fogged), splat.png
   (ground, rock, low, scree; bytes sum to 255), tileset / ground_masks / ground_noise png (runtime shader), heightfield.json,
   props.glb (instanced, clustered: boulder clusters at cliff bases / gullies, debris, spires, shrub clumps, crystal outcrops),
   formations.glb (arches), anchors + fog {color, density, sky} in .terrain.json, renders overview / eye (1.7 m) / wide.
   Options: grid (256), chunks (4), chunk_px (1024), detail_patches (3), mountains {height, wavelength} | false,
   dunes | false, erosion {droplets, thermal, talus} | false, horizon {radius, rings, segments} | false,
   rocks, debris, shrubs, crystals, spires, mesas, cliffs, arches (counts or false), detail {amplitude, wavelength}.
4. Kits: {"action":"rocks","planet":"kethra","kinds":["boulder","rock","slab","shard","pebble","crystal","mesa","arch"]}
   {"action":"asteroids","field":{"shape":"belt","count":600,"inner":600,"outer":900,"thickness":60,"size":[2,40]}}
5. Backdrops: {"action":"skybox","preset":"ember","size":512,"format":"both"} (presets ember tide verdigris void; layers, galaxy, stars {density})
   {"action":"fx","kinds":["sun","flare","debris","dust","lightning"]}
6. info lists presets and stored planets. Conventions: equirect = three.js equirectUv (row 0 north); cube faces px nx py ny pz nz
   (OpenGL / CubeTextureLoader); terrain axes +X east, +Z south, metres. Shaders: art_help {skill:"planets-space"}.

### Topic: fx

COMBAT FX (art_fx): seeded pixel-art effect flipbooks + engine metadata -> exports/<path|fx>/
Every frame is a pure function of (options, seed, t): same input = byte-identical sheet. Colours come from hue-shifted ramps (emission: dark red -> white core; matter: cool shadow -> warm light) with ordered Bayer dither; alpha is 0 or 255 only.
- make {type, variant?, seed?, size? (cell px or [w,h]), frames? (1-64), fps?, hue? (deg, rotates emission ramps), palette? (["#rrggbb"..] | "project:<name>": every colour snapped onto it), name?, group? ("fx"; letters, digits, _ -), path?, canvas? (true | name: open the frames in the UI; overwrite:true replaces an existing canvas)}
  -> <group>/<id>.png (sheet <= 1024 px; square cells use a Roblox grid: 4 frames = 2x2, 16 = 4x4, 64 = 8x8) and the entry in fx.json (groups -> id -> metadata). premultiplied sheets also get <group>/<id>_straight.png (Roblox). File paths in the metadata are relative to the fx folder.
- types / variants:
  muzzle: pistol smg rifle dmr shotgun lmg sniper launcher energy plasma; view side (third person, points +x, pivot at the muzzle) | front_side (3/4 toward the camera: foreshortened flame, the flash-hider star shows) | back_side (3/4 away: the flame tapers into depth) | front (into camera) | fp (screen space, centred on the fp muzzle anchor, flame cone toward the frame centre: aim_deg or anchor:[x,y] + frame_size [384,216]); suppressed:true. Third-person metadata views = the per-facing sprite table {E, W, SE, SW, NE, NW, S, N: {fx:<id>, flip_x?, scale?, behind?}} naming the side / front_side / back_side / front sprites (each drawn for its view, never a scaled side sprite).
  fp aim variants: aims?:5 (default; N 1..9 variants 25 deg apart around the base aim) | [deg, ..] (screen angles) | false (one sheet). Each variant is drawn at its aim (not rotated): <id>.png is the base aim, <id>_aim<i>.png the others; fp.aims = [{aim_deg (ascending), file, straight?}]. Per shot draw the variant whose aim_deg is nearest the muzzle's screen aim (atan2 of anchor -> frame centre, or the socket's screen rotation). preview draws only the anchor's aim.
  tracer: ballistic energy plasma (head at the right edge; stretch along velocity). casing: rifle pistol shotgun (spin loop). dust: mag_drop landing.
  impact: metal concrete stone glass dirt sand water flesh armor shield electronics (sprite up = surface normal, pivot at the hit point).
  decal: all | bullet_metal bullet_concrete bullet_glass bullet_armor bullet_electronics bullet_dirt scorch blood energy_burn (list ok); variants (per kind, 4), size (cell, power of two) -> <group>/<id>.png albedo, <id>_n.png normal (tangent, +Y up), <id>_h.png height (128 = surface), <id>_e.png emissive; cells:{kind:[[x,y,w,h]..]}, material hints (alpha_test, emissive_strength, polygon_offset).
  explosion: frag plasma emp incendiary. smoke: column grenade (color:"#rrggbb") muzzle trail. fire: small large. sparks: shower arc. steam: vent leak (sound: loop steam_vent | steam_leak while it plays + steam_hiss one-shot on start; art_audio recipes). strobe: red amber blue green (mode pulse | beacon). haze: flame sheet (distortion mask: RG offset, A strength). particles: 8x8 cells spark ember glint hex chip shard droplet dust blood smoke.
  Loops (tracer casing smoke column/grenade/trail fire sparks steam strobe haze) are periodic: the last frame flows into the first.
- metadata per effect: blend (additive | alpha | premultiplied: alpha-0 texels add light, 255 occlude | distortion), frames, fps, loop, duration_ms, cell, grid, pivot (+ pivot_uv), facing (camera | camera_up | camera_axis | velocity | surface | screen), size_m, emitters [{cell: particles:<name> | fx:<id>, count, rate_per_s?, velocity {dir, cone_deg, speed_mps}, gravity_mps2, drag, lifetime_s, bounce?, size_over_life, color_over_life, alpha_over_life?}], light {color, radius_m, intensity [[ms, v]], loop?} (dynamic point light), fp {shake {amp_px, freq_hz, decay_ms}, flash {color, alpha, ms}, anchor, events} for first person, sound [art_audio recipe names: art_audio sfx {recipe}], decal (what to stamp), roblox {flipbook, light_emission, file, note}.
- batch {preset: all | muzzle | impact | items:[{type, ...}], seed?, hue?, palette?, group?} = many makes + <group>_contact.png.
- preview {...make options, scale?:3 (1-8; lowered so frames stay <= 1024 px and the strip fits one sheet), over?:{canvas, frame?, anchor?:"socket_muzzle" | [x,y]}} -> previews/<id>.gif + frame strip; over composites the effect on a canvas frame at an anchor (art_model render fp frames store socket_muzzle per frame; its screen rotation becomes aim_deg).
- list = types, variants, weapon classes, surfaces, limits, manifest groups. export {group?} validates every entry (schema, files on disk, PNG size = sheet, <= 1024 px) and writes <group>.fx.json for the game.
three.js:
// three.js (r150+): play one art_fx flipbook from <group>.fx.json
const man = await (await fetch('fx/fx.fx.json')).json(), m = man.effects['muzzle_rifle_side'];
const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('fx/' + m.file);
tex.magFilter = tex.minFilter = THREE.NearestFilter; tex.generateMipmaps = false; tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
tex.repeat.set(m.cell[0] / m.sheet[0], m.cell[1] / m.sheet[1]);
const blending = { additive: THREE.AdditiveBlending, alpha: THREE.NormalBlending, premultiplied: THREE.CustomBlending }[m.blend];
const mat = new THREE.SpriteMaterial({ map: tex, blending, depthWrite: false, transparent: true, alphaTest: m.blend === 'alpha' ? 0.5 : 0 });
if (m.blend === 'premultiplied') { mat.premultipliedAlpha = true; mat.blendSrc = THREE.OneFactor; mat.blendDst = THREE.OneMinusSrcAlphaFactor; } // alpha-0 texels add light, alpha-255 texels occlude
const spr = new THREE.Sprite(mat); spr.center.set(m.pivot_uv[0], 1 - m.pivot_uv[1]); spr.scale.set(m.size_m, m.size_m * m.cell[1] / m.cell[0], 1);
const light = m.light && new THREE.PointLight(m.light.color, 0, m.light.radius_m);
function setFrame(k) { // k = frame index; cells row-major from the top-left
  const c = k % m.grid[0], r = Math.floor(k / m.grid[0]);
  tex.offset.set(c * m.cell[0] / m.sheet[0], 1 - (r + 1) * m.cell[1] / m.sheet[1]);
}
function lightAt(ms) { // piecewise-linear [[ms, intensity]]; loop: ms %= the last key
  const I = m.light.intensity, t = m.light.loop ? ms % I[I.length - 1][0] : ms;
  for (let i = 1; i < I.length; i++) if (t <= I[i][0]) { const a = I[i - 1], b = I[i]; return a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * (t - a[0]) / Math.max(1, b[0] - a[0]); }
  return m.light.loop ? I[0][1] : 0;
}
// each tick: const ms = now - start, k = Math.floor(ms * m.fps / 1000);
// if (!m.loop && k >= m.frames) remove(); else { setFrame(m.loop ? k % m.frames : k); if (light) light.intensity = lightAt(ms); }
// fp muzzle (m.facing "screen"): draw on the HUD / viewmodel layer with the pivot on the frame's muzzle anchor;
// m.fp.shake -> camera shake (amp_px at the 384x216 frame), m.fp.flash -> full-screen tint for flash.ms.
// emitters: spawn extra particles from particles.png cells (m.emitters[i].cell = "particles:spark" etc.).
Roblox: ParticleEmitter.Texture = the sheet (or <id>_straight.png for premultiplied), FlipbookLayout = roblox.flipbook (Grid2x2 / Grid4x4 / Grid8x8; only square sheets, frames = 4 / 16 / 64 for no blank cells), FlipbookMode OneShot (loop: Loop), Lifetime = duration_ms / 1000, LightEmission = roblox.light_emission (1 additive, 0.5 premultiplied fallback, 0 alpha), Size from size_m (studs = m / 0.28), ResampleMode Pixelated on ImageLabels; tracers (non-square) -> Beam with the sheet; decals -> crop cells into Decal / SurfaceAppearance images (no UV rects); dynamic light: PointLight Brightness from light.intensity. Distortion masks have no Roblox equivalent (skip haze).

### Topic: fp

FIRST-PERSON VIEWMODELS (art_fp, the fp v2 runtime contract)
Nothing is baked: arms are animated once per handling class; guns, magazines, attachments and items are sprite sweeps the game turns and snaps at runtime.
1. art_fp kit (optional) -> editable art_model kit: one standard gun per class (built to the class grip geometry from handling.js), magazines, attachments (reflex, scope_4x, suppressor, compensator, vertical_grip, angled_grip), items (knife, baton, riot_shield, frag, medpen, bandage, trauma_kit, tablet). Anchors are sockets: grip, support, mag_well, muzzle, optic, muzzle_mount, underbarrel, sight (+ mount on mags/attachments); moving parts are named nodes with state poses (bolt_back, charging_back, slide_locked, pump_back, bolt_up, cover_open). Kit models use global model names (rifle, reflex, knife, ..., the fp pipeline finds them by name): an existing model with a kit name is kept (reply kept / warning), overwrite:true replaces it.
2. art_fp sweep {out} -> manifest/fp_guns.json, fp_mags.json, fp_attach.json + fp/guns|mags|attach|items/<name>/sweep_<n>.png. Cells: yaw columns x pitch rows, row-major across sheets of <= 1024 px; every anchor listed per cell; one camera for all (frame 384x216, focal 176 px, reference at 34 cm = ~518 px/m). Grids come from the angles the class clips use. State variants: <gun>@<state>; optic lens layers: att:<name>@lens.
3. art_fp batch {out, skins?:[mec, severance], classes?, clips?} -> manifest/fp.json sprite sets fp_<class> (other skins fp_<class>.<skin>) with <anim>_back.png / _front.png strips and per-frame gun / mag / item (item2: a second held item) sockets + events; @vgrip / @agrip variants for smg, rifle, dmr, lmg. Melee clips (gun melee, knife slash / stab / combo, unarmed melee, baton strike / shield_up / shield_bash) add anims.<clip>.melee: hit events, active windows, strike capsules per active frame (art_help topic:"melee").
4. art_fp composite {out, class, clip, frame, gun?, attachments:{optic, muzzle, underbarrel}, yaw_offset?, pitch_offset?} = the frame exactly as the game draws it. art_fp check {out} = hands on every gun's anchors, ADS sight centred, magazine hand-offs, anchor continuity, grip geometry (handling.js conform), attachment fits.
Arms: 3D skeleton in eye space (clavicle, upper arm, forearm, palm, thumb / index / grouped fingers), two-bone IK onto the drawn anchors, finger presets (trigger, support_under, vgrip, agrip, mag_grasp, pinch, pistol_cup, knife_hammer, grenade_hold, pin_pull, open_palm, fist), part sprites per view bucket with RotSprite rotation (palette-stable). Arm pixels behind a prop go to the back layer.
Paint-over: art_fp paint {sweep} (mode:"export", the default) -> canvases; draw; art_fp paint {mode:"import", sweep} writes them back (anchors kept).
HAND-DRAWN (2D, no 3D model): the same files, so the game and composite / check do not change.
- Guns / magazines / attachments / items: art_fp template {kind:gun|mag|attachment|item, name, class, view:hip|ads|reload|side|side_right|rear|three_quarter_rear|three_quarter_front|top (or yaw, pitch, roll), state?, mag?, slot?} -> a canvas (layer "art" + "guides" with the class anchors in that view; meta.fp2d holds source, kind, class, view, anchors). Draw a few keys (2-4: hip, ads, reload cover what the clips use). art_fp anchors {canvas, set:{name:[x,y]}, remove, suggest:true, accept:<min confidence>} places / moves anchors, suggests them from the silhouette (with confidence) and warns when one is off the opaque pixels or more than 2 px from where the other keys put it.
- art_fp sweep2d {out, sources?} -> fp_guns / fp_mags / fp_attach entries like art_fp sweep (+ source:"2d", source2d, check2d: palette, warnings). Each cell = its nearest key warped as a card (plane-induced perspective + a correction field through the drawn anchors), sampled nearest from a Scale2x upscale and re-outlined: source palette only, hard alpha, deterministic. Anchors follow the same warp (exact at a key's own angle). Cells far from every key stay plain cards: add a key or paint them. art_fp paint {mode:"import"} on a 2D sweep keeps painted cells as override canvases (fpo_*), reapplied by the next sweep2d. States: draw keys with state:"bolt_back" -> <gun>@<state>.
- Arms: art_fp template {kind:"arm", name:<skin>, part:upper|fore|hand, view (limbs toward|side|away, hands back|palm|edge), pose (hands: trigger, trigger_off, thumb_release, support, vgrip, agrip, mag_pinch, open, relaxed, fist, grenade, pinch)} -> part canvases with joint/end (limbs) or wrist/grip (hands) points; hands have "back" and "front" layers (behind / over what they hold). art_fp batch {skins:[<skin>]} drives them with the same class clips (IK, finger preset -> pose drawing per frame, thumb_release on mag / slide release events); missing poses and views fall back. art_fp trace {skin:"mec", name} exports a 3D skin as an editable 2D skin. Mixed sets work: 2D gun + 3D arms, 3D gun + 2D arms, all 2D (batch {guns:{smg:"<2D gun>"}}). The all-2D path builds no kit 3D model (only the class anchor table).
- Hands vs the gun (any set with a 2D skin or gun): hand drawings have layers back (palm, far fingers: behind the held object), front (near fingers, thumb) and trigger (the index finger through the guard). Keys carry contact zones: hidden layers mask_grip, mask_guard, mask_fore (guns), mask_pinch (magazines) - paint them, or leave them empty for automatic zones (grip / foregrip around their anchors, the guard = see-through holes near the grip, pinch = the top of the magazine); they warp with the sweep like anchors. Front finger pixels over the gun outside the zones go behind it; the trigger finger shows in the guard opening. Optional "height" layer (grey = cm toward the eye; empty = from the distance to the outline) gives 2D cells per-pixel depth. Batch nudges a hidden hand or one hiding the magazine (fallback pose drawings, half-pixel offsets inside the 1 px tolerance); check fails on finger pixels outside the zones or a magazine in hand less than 50% visible outside its pinch zone, and reports contact_checks, worst.finger_out_px, worst.mag_visible_min.

### Topic: graph

ASSET GRAPH (art_graph): the light index of what is part of what
Orient yourself with it instead of calling art_info on every asset: replies are ids, relation types and one-line notes only (a few hundred chars).
Nodes: a bare name ("helmet_front": canvas, else model, rig, audio, group, project) or kind:name: canvas: rig: model: audio: project: group: palette: export:<path> file:<path>, and sub-assets layer:<canvas>/<layer>, anim:<canvas>/<tag>, frame:<canvas>/<n>, rigpart:<rig>/<part>, modelpart:<model>/<part>.
Automatic (derived from the workspace, never stale): project membership (part_of project:), layers (layer_of), animation tags (part_of), rig parts canvas + parts (part_of rig:), rig animate / model render outputs (rendered_from), model textures and placed models (depends_on), normal maps (variant_of {map:normal}), CTM tilesets (rendered_from), exports (exports_to export:<file>).
You add the semantic ones:
- link {from:"helmet_side", rel:"variant_of", to:"helmet_front", attrs:{view:"side"}}; rels: part_of variant_of view_of layer_of uses_palette rendered_from exports_to depends_on replaces, or a custom lowercase label. unlink {from, rel?, to?} or {node}.
- group {name:"Severance armour", members:["helmet_front","helmet_side"], parent?:"Armour", note?} (groups nest; cycles are refused); remove:[..]; delete:true.
- tag {node, add:["helmet"], remove?}; note {node, note:"one line"} (null clears).
Read:
- summary {} = workspace outline (groups tree, projects, tags); summary {group} = one group as a tree.
- query {node, depth?:1, rel?, dir?:"out"|"in"|"both", limit?:12} = adjacency list ("rel> target" outgoing, "<rel source" incoming, leaf sub-assets grouped on one line).
- find {tag|rel|text|kind} = matching nodes (rel alone lists those edges). path {from, to} = shortest relation chain.
Output is capped (max_chars, default 1600); narrow with rel, depth or limit. The web UI shows the graph live (Graph view).

### Topic: cleanup

CLEANUP (art_cleanup): retire superseded assets without leaving junk or breaking what still uses them
1. replace {old:"marine_old", new:"marine"} (or pairs:[{old,new}]) records "new replaces old", moves old's semantic graph edges (variant_of, group membership, ...) and its OPEN review notes to new, and marks old superseded (its tags stay, to select it).
2. plan {select:{superseded:true}, include_exports:true} = dry run: what goes (count, sizes, first 10), what blocks it, warnings (pinned, still rendered from / variant of a kept asset), export files refused by the path rules. Nothing changes.
3. apply {plan_id, confirm:true} moves exactly the planned assets to <workspace>/trash/<batch>/ (soft delete), with their stored graph edges, tags/notes/approval, review notes (+ images), pins and pruned manifest entries.
4. restore {ids:["t..."]} (a batch) or {ids:["canvas:x"]} (one asset) or {all:true} puts files, edges, notes and pins back exactly. trash lists batches. empty {older_than?:"30d", ids?, confirm:true} is the ONLY hard delete.
select (fields AND together; arrays inside a field OR; an array of selects is a union):
- names:["marine_*", "weapons/rifle/*"] (globs: * = not "/", ** = anything) | ids:[...] | kind:"canvas"|"rig"|"model"|"audio"|"project"|"export" | tag | group (nested groups too) | project | exclude:[globs]
- rel:{rel:"rendered_from", to:"model:rifle_v1"} (assets with that edge to x) or {rel, from} (x's targets)
- superseded:true | orphans:true (no inbound edges, not in a project or group, not pinned) | stale_exports:true (export files whose source asset is gone)
- older_than:"30d" (last edit) | unused_since:"14d" (no edit, export, relation or review since); number = days, or an ISO date.
Export files are only touched when chosen (kind:"export", stale_exports, or include_exports) and only inside workspace/exports or a folder the USER allowlisted (cleanup.allow_paths in <workspace>/config.json, or the web UI); symlinks and paths that resolve outside are refused.
Safety: an asset a kept asset needs (rig parts of a kept rig, a texture of a kept model, the project palette of kept canvases: depends_on, uses_palette, part_of project) blocks the plan; include_dependents:true removes those dependents too ("all" also soft ones like rendered_from), force:true ignores them. Approved assets need allow_approved:true; pinned ones warn.
prune_manifest:{file, keys?:["sprites.marine_idle"]} also removes entries from a JSON manifest (no keys = entries naming a removed export file); the original goes to the trash.
usage = disk use by kind, project and group, biggest offenders, trash size. Replies are compact (counts + first N; limit, full:true).
art_canvas/art_model/art_audio/art_project delete also move the files to the trash (graph and notes unchanged, as before); cleanup.trash_deletes:false in config.json restores hard deletes.

## 5. Skills

art_help {skill:"<name>"} returns each of these; they are also MCP prompts, and `agent-art skills --out DIR` writes them as DIR/agent-art-<name>/SKILL.md.

### Skill: tileable-texture

Description: Makes seamless, tileable pixel-art textures (stone, cobble, bricks, dirt, sand, planks, metal) with Agent Art. Use when asked for a tileable or seamless texture, a Minecraft block texture, or RPG floor and wall tiles. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Tileable block/floor texture (stone, cobble, dirt, wood, metal)
When: Any seamless texture: Minecraft blocks, RPG floor/wall tiles.

1. Canvas + ramp (4-5 shades, hue-shifted):
   art_create_canvas {"name":"cobble","width":16}
   art_palette {"canvas":"cobble","action":"ramp","base":"#8a8a94","steps":5,"prefix":"s"}
2. Surface in ONE command (pick by material):
   - stone/cobble: {"op":"cells","colors":["s0","s1","s2","s3","s4"],"gap_color":"#2e2c36","size":5,"seed":3}
   - bricks: {"op":"cells","colors":["b1","b2","b3"],"gap_color":"#3a2a28","size":4,"stretch":2,"layout":"brick","jitter":0,"profile":"flat","depth":1}
   - dirt/sand: {"op":"noise","colors":["d1","d2","d3"],"weights":[0.3,0.5,0.2],"scale":3,"despeckle":1} then {"op":"scatter","colors":["d4"],"density":0.03}
   - planks: rect bands per plank (h 4), {"op":"bevel","light":"w3","dark":"w0"} per band, a few line grain marks.
3. Hand details with grid (cracks, moss, highlights) — few and deliberate.
4. art_critique {"canvas":"cobble"} -> fix tiling_seam / orphan_pixels / noisy, then art_view {"canvas":"cobble","tile":3}.
5. Variants: art_canvas duplicate + art_draw remap of the ramp.

### Skill: sprite

Description: Draws one pixel-art sprite (hero, enemy, monster, item, prop) with palette ramps, form shading and an outline in Agent Art. Use for a single sprite or icon-sized character; for several views or animations use agent-art-rig. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Character / item / monster sprite
When: A single sprite (hero, enemy, item icon, prop).

1. Size (16/24/32/48) and ramps: one 4-5 shade ramp per material (skin, cloth, metal) + one dark outline color (hue-shifted, not black).
2. Flat silhouette, one mid color per part (head, body, limbs, gear) with rect/ellipse/polygon/grid. Keep it chunky: thin 1px limbs vanish.
3. Form shading per part, one light (top-left):
   {"op":"shade","colors":["r0","r1","r2","r3","r4"],"of":"r2"}  (or per_color:true over the whole sprite when each part has its own flat color — then remap each part to its ramp)
4. {"op":"outline","color":"#2a1a22"}  (outer). Optional: inner lines between parts with grid.
5. Face/details by hand with grid rows: eyes (2px), highlight pixels on metal, belt, buttons.
6. art_critique {"canvas":"hero"} (pillow_shading, weak_outline, orphan_pixels, too_many_colors) -> fix -> art_view.
Multiple views or animations of this sprite -> use the "rig" skill so it stays identical.

### Skill: rig

Description: Builds a rigged pixel-art character or creature (humanoid, blob, flyer or custom) whose parts are drawn once and tweened into side, front and back views and animations (walk, idle, attack, jump, death). Use whenever a sprite needs more than one direction or frame. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Consistent character: views (front/side/back) + animations from one rig
When: A character/creature needed in several directions or animations (walk, idle, attack) — keeps it the SAME everywhere.

Fast path (any humanoid, blob/slime, bat/bird): a template is a starting point you can reshape:
   art_rig {"action":"create","name":"knight","frame":[32,32],"template":"humanoid","parts":{"head":{"w":12,"h":10},"cape":{"w":8,"h":12,"pivot":[4,0],"parent":"body","at":[-2,-6],"z":-4}}}
   draw every listed cell (step 2), art_rig preview, then one call per animation:
   art_rig {"action":"animate","name":"knight","preset":"walk","view":"side"}  -> tag "walk_side" on canvas "knight" (preset tags are always <preset>_<view>; animation:"<name>" picks your own; override any field: frames, fps, keys, loop)
High-detail character (64x96 .. 160x240, 8 directions, IK, foot planting, follow-through): use the "rig-hd" skill (template:"humanoid_hd").
Custom rig (anything else: quadrupeds, vehicles, props with moving parts):
1. Create the rig (parts are drawn once per view; frames are generated from them):
   art_rig {"action":"create","name":"knight","frame":[32,32],"views":["side","front","back"],"parts":{"body":{"w":12,"h":12,"pivot":[6,10]},"head":{"w":12,"h":12,"pivot":[6,11],"parent":"body","at":[0,-9]},"arm_f":{"w":5,"h":9,"pivot":[2,1],"parent":"body","at":[2,-8],"z":2},"arm_b":{"w":5,"h":9,"pivot":[2,1],"parent":"body","at":[-2,-8],"z":-1},"leg_f":{"w":5,"h":8,"pivot":[2,1],"parent":"body","at":[1,0],"z":1},"leg_b":{"w":5,"h":8,"pivot":[2,1],"parent":"body","at":[-2,0],"z":-2}},"root":[16,22]}
2. The reply (and art_rig info) lists the part cells on the "<name>_parts" canvas compactly: cells.rows = the y of each view's band, cells.parts = [x, w, h] per part, so a part's cell in a view is [x, rows[view], w, h] (full:true returns the complete JSON). Draw every part in every view there with art_draw (flat colors -> shade -> outline), using the SAME palette keys. Pivot (red dot) = the joint. Mirror views (mirror:{side_left:"side"}) are generated, not drawn.
3. Key poses (offset px and rotation degrees per part, relative to the rest pose):
   art_rig {"action":"pose","name":"knight","pose":"walk_contact","parts":{"leg_f":{"rot":-25},"leg_b":{"rot":25},"arm_f":{"rot":20},"arm_b":{"rot":-20}}}
   art_rig {"action":"pose","name":"knight","pose":"walk_pass","parts":{"body":{"y":-1},"leg_f":{"rot":5},"leg_b":{"rot":-5}}}
4. Animate (tweened in-betweens, any fps):
   art_rig {"action":"animate","name":"knight","animation":"walk","view":"side","keys":[{"pose":"walk_contact"},{"pose":"walk_pass"},{"pose":"walk_contact","mirror_pairs":true},{"pose":"walk_pass"}],"frames":8,"fps":10,"loop":true,"plant_feet":true}
5. art_rig preview {name} (all views + a pose) and art_critique {canvas:"knight", animation:"walk"} (volume_drift, ground_line). Export with art_animation export.

### Skill: rig-hd

Description: Builds a high-detail humanoid_hd character rig (64x96 to 160x240, 8 directions) with per-view poses, two-bone IK, foot planting and cape follow-through. Use for detailed, pre-rendered-style or shooter characters with many smooth animations. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# High-detail character rig (humanoid_hd: 8 directions, per-view poses, IK, foot planting, follow-through)
When: Detailed characters at 64x96 .. 160x240 (late-90s pre-rendered look, shooters, action games) that need many smooth animations in several directions.

1. Create from the template (sizes scale with the frame; cape/gear_hip follow-through, RotSprite sampling and scale_children are already on):
   art_rig {"action":"create","name":"soldier","frame":[128,192],"template":"humanoid_hd","secondary":{"cape":{"stiffness":0.15,"damping":0.2,"gravity":0.5}}} (merged over the template's cape/gear_hip springs)
   Parts: pelvis (root), torso, chest, neck, head (+head:blink), upper_arm/forearm/hand and thigh/shin/foot _f (near) / _b (far), slots weapon (child of hand_f), gear_back, gear_hip, cape. Remove a slot with parts:{cape:null}.
2. Draw every cell in the 5 drawn views (side faces RIGHT, front_side, front, back_side, back) on "soldier_parts"; the _left views are mirrors. The reply gives cells.rows (band y per view) and cells.parts ([x, w, h]): a cell is [x, rows[view], w, h]. Pivot = joint at the top of each limb part; let limb cells overlap the joint a few px so bent knees and elbows stay closed. Draw *_b darker. Check: art_rig {"action":"preview","name":"soldier","pose":"walk_contact"}
3. Presets, one canvas per preset and view (a frame strip is at most 8192 px tall):
   art_rig {"action":"animate","name":"soldier","preset":"walk","view":"front_side","canvas":"soldier_walk_front_side"}
   presets: idle walk run crouch_walk aim shoot reload hurt death throw blink (planting, IK and secondary are set in them). Tags are <preset>_<view>: this one is "walk_front_side".
4. Fix a pose in one view only (merged over the base pose there; mirror views follow their source):
   art_rig {"action":"pose","name":"soldier","pose":"aim","merge":true,"views":{"front":{"head":{"rot":0}}}}
   Forward swings in front/back views: override rot with sy foreshortening, e.g. views:{front:{thigh_f:{rot:0, sy:0.8}}}.
5. Two-bone IK in a pose or key: ik:{end:{target:[x,y] (frame px) | {part, at:[dx,dy]}, bend:1 (knees) | -1 (elbows), rot? (world rot of the end: keep a gun level), weight?}}:
   art_rig {"action":"pose","name":"soldier","pose":"brace","parts":{"chest":{"rot":-4}},"ik":{"hand_b":{"target":{"part":"weapon","at":[20,-3]},"bend":-1}}}
6. Custom cycle with planted feet and follow-through:
   art_rig {"action":"animate","name":"soldier","animation":"patrol","view":"side","keys":[{"pose":"walk_contact"},{"pose":"walk_pass"},{"pose":"walk_contact","mirror_pairs":true},{"pose":"walk_pass","mirror_pairs":true}],"frames":16,"fps":12,"plant":true,"secondary":true,"canvas":"soldier_patrol_side"}
   plant:["foot_f"] picks feet; secondary:{gear_hip:{stiffness:0.4, damping:0.5}} inline uses only these springs for this call.
7. Limbs look jagged or change thickness: rig sampling "rotsprite" (default here) or "smooth"; art_rig update {name, sampling}. art_critique {canvas, animation} for drift, then art_animation export {format:"spritesheet"} (json:false skips the sidecar). Guide: docs/rig-hd-guide.md, art_help {topic:"rig"}.
Armed characters: use the "weapon-handling" skill (hands on grips in every frame and view, carry states, validation).

### Skill: weapon-handling

Description: Makes characters hold guns correctly: both hands on the grips, carry states (aim, ready, sprint, reload, holster), reach, no clipping and draw order, with validation, for 2D rigs and first-person arms. Use for any armed character or viewmodel with a rifle, SMG, shotgun, pistol or attachments. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Characters holding guns: grips, carry states, reach, dead zone, validation (2D rigs and FP arms)
When: Any character sprite or first-person arms holding a rifle, SMG, shotgun, DMR, LMG or pistol, including attachments (vertical / angled grip, bipod, suppressor), in every direction and animation.

2D characters (art_rig, humanoid_hd):
1. Create with the weapon declared (cell sized for the class; attachment cells added):
   art_rig {"action":"create","name":"soldier","frame":[128,192],"template":"humanoid_hd","weapon":{"class":"rifle","attachments":{"vgrip":"vertical_grip"}}}
2. Draw the weapon and att_vgrip in the SIDE row only, pointing right (stock left, pistol grip ~30% in, handguard / muzzle right). The other views project that cell (canted outward with a length floor where the barrel points at the camera).
3. Check the hold: art_rig {"action":"preview","name":"soldier","pose":"idle_exhale","carry":"aim"} then art_rig {"action":"check","name":"soldier"} (every preset x 8 views: hands on grips, reach, elbows, penetration, muzzle, layering, visibility).
4. Animate as usual: presets carry the weapon (walk = ready_low, run = sprint, aim / shoot = aim with cheek weld (front view: short barrel canted toward the centre line), reload = mag out -> chest pouch -> mag in -> charging handle with events (draw the "mag" cell in the side row too), throw = slung, death drops it). Per call: carry:"ready_high", attach:[] (no attachment), variant:"heavy" (equipment set). animate refuses violating frames by default; constraints:"fix" auto-corrects, "warn" writes and reports.
5. Tune: weapon.points {grip_main:{at:[x,y], angle}, grip_support, stock, muzzle, optic, mag} in weapon-cell px; weapon.states {name:{base:"ready_low", angle:30}}; weapon.layer {pin:{side:"front"}} for draw order; art_rig {"action":"layers","name":"soldier","preset":"walk","frame":3,"view":"side"} / explain {part_a:"chest", part_b:"weapon"} to see why.
6. Left-handed beat or shoulder switch: key mirror_hands:true. mirror_pairs keeps the held hands on their side.
First-person (art_model):
1. art_model {"action":"create","name":"ar","template":"fp_rifle","weapon":{"attach":["vertical_grip"]}} and create {name:"arms", template:"fp_arms"}.
2. art_model {"action":"render","name":"arms","canvas":"arms_aim","size":[160,120],"camera":"fp","hold":{"weapon":"ar","carry":"aim"}} (hands on the grips, optic on the eye line); render the gun layer with hold:{arms:"arms", carry:"aim"} so both layers match.
3. art_model {"action":"check","name":"arms","hold":{"weapon":"ar"}} validates every clip x carry state; animate {name:"arms", clip:"reload_empty", hold:{weapon:"ar", carry:"reload", bake_weapon:"reload_empty_held"}} bakes held clips for glTF.

### Skill: anim-library

Description: Authors motion once on a skeleton and renders it on many skins and loadouts (art_anim), batching game sprite strips and a characters manifest, with optional runtime gun layers. Use for a roster of characters that share a clip library, for retargeting, or for exporting every animation to a game. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Animation library: one skeleton + clip library, many skins, batch render to game strips + manifest
When: Several characters (factions, armour sets, body types) sharing the same motion set, or rendering a whole character roster for a game manifest.

1. Skeleton (rig definition + the standard clips): art_anim {"action":"skeleton","name":"hd","template":"humanoid_hd","frame":[128,192],"weapon":{"class":"rifle"},"proportions":{"heavy":{"width":1.15,"spine":1.04},"lean":{"width":0.9,"legs":1.04}}}
2. One skin per character: art_anim {"action":"skin","name":"mec","skeleton":"hd","proportions":"heavy"} creates rig "mec" with cells sized for its proportions. Draw the cells (art_rig info {name:"mec"} lists them). Linked cells save work: parts.<p>.link:{back_side:"side"}; art_rig derive {name:"mec", from:"side", to:["front_side"]} copies a view to paint over.
3. Check the drawing before rendering: art_rig {"action":"consistency","name":"mec"} (views agree: palette, bone lengths, joints, silhouette) and art_rig {"action":"zcheck","name":"mec"} (no z-flicker, arm order agrees with depth).
4. New motion once for everyone: art_anim clip {skeleton:"hd", name:"walk_aim", layers:[{clip:"walk"}, {clip:"aim", mask:"upper"}]} (layers + masks), {name:"limp", layers:[{clip:"walk"}, {clip:"flinch", additive:true}]} (additive), events:[{t:0.5, name:"step"}]. Preview on a skin: art_anim {"action":"render","skin":"mec","clip":"walk_aim","view":"front"}.
5. Equipment: skin {equipment:{helmet:{variant:"helmet"}, pack:{part:"gear_back"}}, loadouts:{light:{equip:["helmet"]}, heavy:{equip:["helmet","pack"]}}}.
6. Ship it: art_anim {"action":"batch","skins":["mec","sev"],"loadouts":"all","out":"C:/game/public/assets","front":"auto"} -> characters/<set>/<clip>_<view>.png (+ __front), manifest/characters.json (frame grown by pad:"auto" to fit the barrel, anchor, events, per-frame draw order).
6b. Guns drawn by the game (runtime weapon layers): art_anim {"action":"batch","skins":["mec"],"out":"C:/game/public/assets","weapon":"runtime"} (gun-free body + __front strips, per-frame sockets); one asset per gun: art_anim {"action":"weapon","name":"ar","class":"rifle","skin":"mec"} (draw it), conform {weapon:"ar"}, weapon_sheet {weapon:"ar", out} (weapons_world sheet + manifest), composite {skin:"mec", weapon:"ar", clip:"walk_aim", view:"front"} to see it, weapon_check {skin:"mec"} = hands on the grips of every rifle-class gun.
7. Other engines: art_anim gltf {skin:"mec", clips:["walk","reload"]} (skinned cutout mesh + animations). Another skeleton: art_anim retarget {clip:"walk", from:"hd", to:"hd_small"}.

### Skill: walk-cycle

Description: Hand-animates a short frame-by-frame walk cycle for an existing pixel sprite without a rig. Use for a quick 4-frame walk or bob; for 8+ frames or several directions use agent-art-rig. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Walk cycle without a rig (frame-by-frame)
When: Quick hand-drawn animation of an existing sprite.

1. art_animation {"canvas":"hero","action":"insert","count":3,"copy_from":0}  -> 4 identical frames to edit.
2. Poses: 0 contact (legs apart), 1 down (body 1px lower), 2 contact mirrored, 3 up (body 1px higher). Only redraw legs/arms per frame: art_draw {frame:N, commands:[clear the leg area, grid new legs]}.
3. Keep head/torso pixels identical (copy from_frame 0) and the feet on the same ground row.
4. art_animation {"canvas":"hero","action":"tag","name":"walk","from":0,"to":3,"duration":120}; check art_view {frame, onion:1} and art_critique (volume_drift, ground_line).
For 8+ frames or several directions use the rig skill.

### Skill: iso-scene

Description: Builds a 2:1 isometric pixel-art scene (tactics map, room, courtyard) from iso tiles and boxes with light and shadow layers. Use when asked for an isometric map, diorama or iso tiles. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Isometric scene (tactics map, room, courtyard)
When: 2:1 pixel isometric dioramas.

1. Canvas e.g. 160x120 with a background gradient; origin = top vertex of cell 0,0 (e.g. [80,24]), tile 32.
2. Floor back to front: {"op":"iso_tile","at":[0,0,0],"tile":32,"origin":[80,24],"color":"#6a7a5a","outline":"#2a3326","inset":1} for each cell (increasing gx+gy).
3. Blocks/props back to front: {"op":"iso_box","at":[1,1,0],"tile":32,"origin":[80,24],"height":16,"top":"#b89a72","outline":"#3a2a20","edge":"#e0c79c"}; small props with w:16 anchor:"center".
4. Texture faces with mask:<face color> (noise/scatter/grid), props as separate canvases stamped with copy from_canvas.
5. Light layer: art_layer add {blend:"screen"} + light / glow; shadows with cast_shadow or a multiply layer.
6. art_layer stamp_visible + quantize; art_critique {kind:"scene"}.

### Skill: hd2d-scene

Description: Paints a layered 2.5D / HD-2D pixel-art scene: sky, parallax far / mid / foreground layers, light rays, fog, glow and vignette. Use for backgrounds, title screens and atmospheric scenes. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# 2.5D / HD-2D scene (parallax layers, light, fog)
When: Backgrounds, title screens, atmospheric scenes.

1. Layers bottom->top: sky (gradient), far (silhouettes, low contrast, bluish), mid, play, foreground. art_layer add {position:"top"} each.
2. Far layers: shapes + adjust lightness/saturation down; blur radius 1 optional.
3. Light: layer blend "screen": rays from the light source, light at lamps/windows; shadows: layer blend "multiply".
4. fog {direction:"up", to:0.4, steps:0} between far and mid layers; glow {gain:3} on emissive pixels.
5. art_layer stamp_visible -> quantize {dither:"bayer"} on the stamp -> vignette.
6. art_critique {kind:"scene"}, art_view.

### Skill: minecraft-pack

Description: Makes a Minecraft Java resource pack: textures under the real vanilla names and sizes, animated textures, and the built pack zip. Use when asked for Minecraft block or item textures or a resource pack. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Minecraft resource pack
When: Making block/item textures for a Minecraft Java version.

1. art_project create {name, meta:{minecraft:"1.12.2", pack:"my-pack"}, palette, notes (style rules)}.
2. art_minecraft vanilla {version:"1.12.2", filter:"stone|planks"} -> real names/sizes (1.12: blocks/planks_oak; 1.13+: block/oak_planks).
3. One canvas per texture with meta.texture (e.g. "blocks/stone"), using the tileable-texture skill; animated ones with frames + meta.frametime.
4. Grass/leaves: grayscale + meta.tint for previews.
5. Review the whole set: art_sheet {project, tile:3}. Then art_minecraft build {project}.

### Skill: 3d-kit

Description: Builds a modular HD-2D 3D environment kit (floors, walls, arches, stairs, ruins, dioramas) and extruded or lathed props from pixel textures, exported as .glb. Use for low-poly 3D map pieces with pixel-art textures, connected textures (CTM) or moss and grime overlays. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# HD-2D 3D environment kit (modular pieces -> .glb) and props
When: Map environments for a 3D game in the HD-2D look (pixel textures on low-poly meshes): floors, walls, arches, stairs, ruins, dioramas; also extruded/lathed props.

1. Tileable textures at the game density (32 px = 1 unit = one grid cell), using the tileable-texture skill:
   art_create_canvas {"name":"stone","width":32}  -> cells/noise, check art_view tile:3.  Also e.g. "floor_tile", "cap" (wall top), "grime" (mostly transparent dirt for overlays), "crack" (a transparent canvas with painted cracks = holes mask).
2. One model per kit piece (pieces snap on the 32 px grid; textures repeat at 1 texel = 1 px so neighbours line up). Each new model is baked onto ONE atlas canvas <name>_uv (world-aligned texture + contact AO, edge wear, grime), so its parts read as one object; unwrap:false keeps per-part textures:
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"wall_a","parts":[{"type":"wall","w":32,"h":64,"d":8,"texture":{"canvas":"stone","overlay":"grime"},"top":"cap"}],"preview":true}
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"arch_a","parts":[{"type":"arch","span":24,"spring":20,"d":8,"texture":"stone"}]}
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"floor_a","parts":[{"type":"floor","texture":"floor_tile"}]}
   Ruined variants: {"type":"wall","texture":"stone","broken":{"amount":24,"step":4,"seed":3},"holes":"crack"}, arch with broken:true, plus {"type":"rubble","count":10,"texture":"stone","at":[0,0,12]}.
   Others: corner, pillar, column, vault, stairs {steps, rise, run, tread}, ledge, balustrade, roof {style: gable|shed}. Ships/vehicles: wedge, box taper|bevel|insets, cone, loft {scale_end}, mirror:"x", glass:true, origin:"bottom". art_help {topic:"3d"} lists every option.
3. Look: art_model {"action":"preview","name":"wall_a"} (game = the 38° game camera, plus front/side/top/iso). Iterate with update {"action":"update","name":"wall_a","set":{"0":{"h":96}}}.
4. Export each piece: art_model {"action":"export","name":"wall_a"} -> exports/wall_a.glb + wall_a.meta.json. Z-up engine: object.rotation.x = Math.PI/2, or up:"z".
5. Diorama section from placed pieces (cell = grid coords, turn = 90° steps):
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"crypt_a","parts":[{"type":"model","model":"floor_a","array":{"count":4,"cell_step":[1,0,0]}},{"type":"model","model":"wall_a","cell":[0,0,-1]},{"type":"model","model":"arch_a","cell":[1,0,-1]}]}
   preview {views:["game"], size:512}; export bakes one .glb (instances:true = shared meshes + nodes). UVs are computed in world space after placement, so the stone continues across every piece.
6. Connected textures (CTM) and decay:
   Marble floor groups: art_model {"action":"ctm","name":"marble_ctm","ctm":{"base":"marble","method":"full","border":{"width":2,"style":"bevel"}}} then floors use texture:"marble_ctm" (border only around each connected group).
   Wall trims: ctm {base:"trim", method:"horizontal"} on a ledge run; random {weights:[6,1,1], variants:[...]} for cracked blocks; repeat (base 96x64 = 3x2 cells) for big slab patterns.
   Moss / grime / wear: {"type":"wall","texture":"stone","overlays":[{"texture":"grime","where":["bottom","corners"],"falloff":20},{"texture":"moss","where":"top","falloff":10}]} (own UV set, cut out by strength).
7. The atlas (column_a -> canvas column_a_uv): paint transitions on its "paint" layer (art_draw), or in a view: art_model {"action":"unwrap","name":"column_a","unwrap":{"do":"view","view":"front"}} then do:"project". unwrap:{do:"check"} reports detached parts; art_model {"action":"unwrap","name":"old_piece"} converts a model saved before (or with unwrap:false). Layouts of placed models (step 5) keep per-part textures so pieces stay instanced.
Props: extrude {"type":"extrude","canvas":"barrel","depth":6}; relief: depth_map:"<height canvas>"; lathe {"type":"lathe","canvas":"candle","segments":12} (draw the RIGHT half from x=0; flame on an "emissive" layer).
Keep pieces light (< 500 tris), reuse a few textures, characters stay 2D billboards.

### Skill: ship-model

Description: Models a low-poly spaceship or vehicle (lofted hull, wedges, cones, canopy, engines, inset panels, mirrored parts) with pixel textures and exports it as .glb. Use for ships, fighters, cars, tanks, drones or turrets as standalone 3D models. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Spaceship / vehicle 3D model (low-poly + pixel textures -> .glb)
When: Ships, fighters, dropships, cars, tanks, turrets, drones: standalone 3D models with hulls, wings, canopies, engines and panels.

1. Textures: a tileable hull plate (32x32, cells/noise + panel lines) and small decals (an "emissive" layer for lights and engine glow):
   art_create_canvas {"name":"hull","width":32}  -> tileable-texture skill.
2. Build with origin:"bottom" (centred, sits on y=0). Y-up, +z = nose, units px (32 px = 1 unit). mirror:"x" makes the other side:
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"scout","origin":"bottom","preview":true,"parts":[{"type":"loft","points":[[-12,0],[12,0],[10,10],[-10,10]],"d":64,"scale_end":[0.3,0.4],"texture":"hull"},{"type":"wedge","w":40,"h":3,"d":24,"top_w":8,"shift":[16,0],"at":[14,2,0],"mirror":"x"},{"type":"cone","r":3,"h":8,"rotate":[90,0,0],"at":[0,5,32]},{"type":"cylinder","r_bottom":5,"r_top":4,"h":10,"rotate":[-90,0,0],"at":[10,5,-32],"mirror":"x"},{"type":"box","w":10,"h":6,"d":14,"bevel":2,"glass":true,"color":"#9fd8ff","at":[0,10,8]},{"type":"box","w":6,"h":6,"d":6,"at":[0,0,-20],"insets":[{"face":"back","rect":[1,1,4,4],"depth":3,"texture":"#f80"}]}]}
3. Pieces: loft (a shape whose far section is scaled by scale_end: hulls, fuselages), shape plane:"zy" (side profile [z,y], extruded along x), wedge (top_w, top_d:0 = ridge, shift:[x,z]: wings, fins, ramps), box taper:[sx,sy] (nose) | bevel:px | insets:[{face, rect:[u,v,w,h], depth}] (>0 recess: intakes, hatches; <0 raised panel; touching an edge = hangar mouth), only one of taper|bevel|insets per box. cylinder r_top/r_bottom (nozzles), cone, wrap:"once" + u_offset (turns) for a decal round a tank.
4. Transforms: scale, rotate:[x,y,z] (deg, X then Y then Z), turn, all about the part origin or pivot:[x,y,z] (hinges, wing roots), then at. Radial arrays: array:{count:6, rotate:[0,60,0], about:[0,0,0]} (engine rings, rotor blades). Canopies, visors, shields: glass:true or opacity:0..1 (glTF BLEND).
5. Look and iterate: art_model {"action":"preview","name":"scout"}, update {set:{0:{d:72}}} / add / remove. Keep it light (< 1000 tris). The ship is baked onto one atlas scout_uv (contact AO, edge wear; re-baked on update; glass keeps its material); unwrap:false = per-part textures.
6. Export: art_model {"action":"export","name":"scout"} -> exports/scout.glb (up:"z" for Z-up engines). Options and recipes: art_help {topic:"3d"}.

### Skill: hard-surface

Description: Adds sci-fi hard-surface detail to .glb models: greebles, pipes and cables, trim sheets, PBR metal / rough, pixel-correct height normals, baked AO, LODs, impostors and collision proxies. Use for hull sections, stations, corridors and city blocks that must look rich and stay fast in a browser. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Hard-surface sci-fi detail: greebles, trim sheets, PBR, normals, baked AO, LODs + impostors (.glb)
When: Big-budget sci-fi look at a pixel-texture budget: ship hull sections, stations, carrier corridors, city blocks; anything that needs greebles, pipes, panel trims, metal/rough, contact shadows, and must stay fast in a browser.

1. Textures with surface data layers (left out of the colour): a 32x32 hull plate with panel lines, then layers "height" (white = high: grooves black, rivets white), "metal" and "rough" (grey = value):
   art_create_canvas {"name":"hull","width":32}; art_layer {"canvas":"hull","action":"add","name":"height"} (and "metal", "rough") -> art_draw on each layer. Canvas-wide PBR instead of layers: art_canvas {"canvas":"hull","action":"meta","meta":{"material":"painted_metal"}}.
2. One trim sheet for edges, seams, pipes, hazard and light strips: art_model {"action":"trim","canvas":"hull_trim"} (or strips:{name:[y,h]} on your own sheet).
3. Hull section: art_model {"action":"create","name":"hull_a","origin":"bottom","parts":[{"type":"box","id":"hull","w":160,"h":40,"d":96,"bevel":3,"texture":"hull","material":"painted_metal","trim":"hull_trim:bevel","greebles":[{"face":"top","seed":11,"grid":2,"density":0.35,"avoid":[[64,0,32,96]]},{"face":"right","seed":12,"density":0.3,"size":[2,8],"kinds":{"vent":3,"pipe":2,"bolts":2,"panel":3}}]},{"type":"box","w":52,"h":22,"d":30,"at":[0,0,36],"boolean":"subtract","target":"hull"},{"type":"tube","path":[[-82,30,44],[-82,30,-40],[-60,30,-46]],"r":2,"trim":"hull_trim:pipe","mirror":"x"},{"type":"tube","from":[-12,50,30],"to":[-12,50,-30],"sag":3,"r":0.6,"sides":4,"color":"#24272c"},{"type":"cylinder","r_bottom":9,"r_top":7,"h":14,"rotate":[-90,0,0],"at":[-50,20,-48],"mirror":"x","color":"#4a4f57","material":"bare_metal"}]}
4. Corridor module (one trim sheet everywhere): floor {texture:"deck"} + a grate strip box {h:0.5, trim:{sheet:"hull_trim", strip:"grate", faces:"all"}}; walls box {insets:[{face:"right", rect, depth:1.5}]}; ribs box {bevel:1, material:"bare_metal", trim:"hull_trim:rib"} every 32 px; ceiling light strip {trim:{sheet:"hull_trim", strip:"light", faces:"all"}}; wall greeble part {w:20, d:110, rotate:[0,0,-90], mirror:"x"}; pipe runs and sagging cables (tube); a bulkhead doorway = box {boolean:"subtract", target:"bulkhead"}.
5. Look: art_model {"action":"preview","name":"hull_a","views":["game"],"ao":true} (also lod:1|2, morph:{open:1}). Iterate seeds, density, avoid rects. A section under 6000 triangles is baked onto one atlas hull_a_uv (contact AO, edge wear; unwrap:false = per-part); bigger ones keep per-part textures (art_model unwrap {name, unwrap:{parts:["hull"]}} bakes the hero part).
6. Export for the browser: art_model {"action":"export","name":"hull_a","bake_ao":true,"lods":[1,0.5,0.2],"impostor":{"grid":8,"size":64},"collision":"hull","occluder":"boxes"}: AO lightmap (TEXCOORD_1), <name>_lods > LOD0..2 with switch distances (THREE.LOD), impostor atlas + json, hidden collision / occluder nodes. Repeated greebles: greeble {instanced:true} -> EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing (InstancedMesh).
7. Interiors: layout model with cull:{rooms:[{name, min, max}, ...]} -> room_<name> nodes, auto doorways, meta.cull.pvs. Budget: 3-8k tris per hero section at LOD0, < 1k per kit piece.

### Skill: ships-structures

Description: Builds original sci-fi ships with walkable interiors, industrial exteriors, mining colonies, neon markets and megastructures from templates, hull curves and kits (art_model), with player-metric checks and triangle budgets. Use for gunships, fighters, dropships, haulers, capital ships, ship interiors or sci-fi set pieces. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Sci-fi ships, ship interiors, industrial exteriors, underground cities and megastructures (.glb, pixel textures)
When: Big-budget sci-fi set pieces at a PSX pixel-texture budget for a browser game (later Roblox): fighters, dropships, haulers, capital ring modules, ship interiors that fit the hull, mining colonies, neon market districts, stations. Designs stay ORIGINAL (no real ship designs, names or marks).

0. Hero / walkable ship at true scale (32 px = 1 m): art_model {"action":"create","name":"tern","template":"gunship"} then {"action":"walk_check","name":"tern"} (player metrics: doors 1.2 x 2.1 m, corridors 1.4 x 2.3 m, stairs 0.2 m, ramps 20 deg) and {"action":"export","name":"tern","static":"landed","lods":[1,0.5,0.25],"split":true,"walk":true}. Your own: hull {shell:6, openings:[{t, u}]} + glazing / ring_door in the openings + interior parts tagged inside:"<hull id>" (portal_arch, locker_wall, pilot_seat, screen_arm, decals) + walk markers; preview mood + ao, a figure for scale.
1. Kit textures + trim sheet once: art_model {"action":"kit"} (kit_hull, kit_deck, kit_wall, kit_screen, kit_glow, kit_hazard, kit_rock, ... with height / metal / rough / emissive layers).
2. Ship from a template (original, seeded), then refine by part name:
   art_model {"action":"create","name":"vk7","template":"fighter","seed":7,"textures":"kit"} (dropship | hauler {bays} | capital_ring {radius, segments}; rigged:false = one static mesh, canopy:"open", gear:"up", ramp:"open")
   art_model {"action":"update","name":"vk7","set":{"wings":{"span":120,"dihedral":6}}}; info lists every part, node and clip (canopy_open, gear_retract, gear_deploy, wings_fold, ramp_open, ...).
3. Hull by hand (design curves): {"type":"hull","id":"hull","length":480,"plan":[[0,30],[0.4,56],[0.85,18],[1,2]],"profile":[[0,40,6],[0.5,50,0],[1,18,14]],"sections":[[0,"hex"],[0.9,"wedge"]],"panel_lines":{"every":64,"seams":[0.17]},"plates":[{"t":[0.3,0.5],"u":[0.2,0.3],"lift":1.2}],"texture":"kit_hull","groove":"kit_metal_dark"}
   Components ride the surface: {"type":"engine","on_hull":{"hull":"hull","t":0.02,"u":0.2,"mirror":true},"rotate":[-90,0,0],"r":16}, {"type":"canopy","name":"canopy","on_hull":{"hull":"hull","t":0.72,"u":0}}, landing_gear {name, at} (contact socket), ramp, cargo_door, wing / fin, turret / rotary_cannon / hardpoint, antenna, sensor_dome, rcs_quad, intake, vent, armor_plate, container_rack. Named = animated nodes + clips; unnamed = static (open / deployed state).
4. Livery: art_model {"action":"livery","name":"vk7","primary":"#6e7682","secondary":"#2f343b","stripes":[{"t":[0.6,0.64],"color":"#b8462e"}],"decals":[{"text":"VK-07","t":0.45}],"mark":{"t":0.18,"seed":11},"wear":0.4} (paint masks, hazard, stencils, an original seeded emblem, scratches; mapped once over the hull). Ship templates are over the automatic atlas size, so they keep per-part textures (create says so in unwrap_note).
5. Look: preview {"action":"preview","name":"vk7","views":[{"yaw":35,"pitch":24,"perspective":true,"fov":30}],"size":384,"mood":true} (dark scene lit by its own engines / lights), pose / clip previews as usual.
6. Interior that fits: art_model {"action":"generate","kind":"interior","name":"vk7_int","hull":"dropship","textures":{"floor":"kit_deck","wall":"kit_wall"}} -> rooms on a corridor spine, doors at the exterior ramp / hatches (report.alignment), windows written back onto the ship, cull rooms. Rooms by hand: corridor {kind:"T"}, room {cells, openings}, door {name}, airlock, ladder, lift, bridge, engine_room, quarters, cargo_bay, hangar, med_bay, armoury, console (MFD screen markers for UI textures), seat.
7. Places: generate {"kind":"mining_colony","name":"colony","seed":9} / {"kind":"market","name":"market","seed":4} (instanced kit models <name>_k_*); kit by hand: tower, dish, tank, silo, crane, gantry, pipeline, scaffold, truss, catwalk, landing_pad, hangar_shell, hab_module, rock_platform, shaft, atrium, bridge_walk, lift_shaft, cable_web, pipe_wall, market_stall, sign_frame, neon {text}, sign, holo, light, fog_card, god_ray.
8. Budget + export: art_model {"action":"budget","name":"vk7"} (class, LOD estimate, draw calls, costliest parts); export {"action":"export","name":"vk7","static":"rest","lods":[1,0.5,0.2],"split":true,"budget":"fighter"} (rigged ships: export without static keeps nodes + clips); layouts: export {"action":"export","name":"colony","instances":true,"collision":"boxes"}. Lights / sockets / doors / screens come out as empty nodes with extras.

### Skill: fp-weapon

Description: Builds a first-person gun and arms as a rigid 3D rig (art_model fp_rifle / fp_pistol / fp_arms) with fire and reload clips and sockets, exported as an animated .glb or rendered to pixel sprite layers with per-frame hand anchors. Use for an FPS viewmodel; for the sprite-composed art_fp pipeline see art_help {topic:"fp"}. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# First-person weapon + arms: 3D rig with clips (.glb) or pre-rendered pixel sprites
When: FPS viewmodels: a gun with moving parts (magazine, bolt, slide) and separate arms, either shipped as true 3D (glTF animations, Roblox Motor6D) or rendered to 2D sprite layers with per-frame hand anchors.

1. Textures first: small tileable canvases (32 px = 1 m; a slot also takes a colour). Texture canvases must exist before create:
   art_create_canvas {"name":"gun_metal","width":16,"height":16,"background":"#2c2e33"} (also gun_poly, sleeve, glove; then noise / cells, tileable-texture skill)
2. Gun rig from a template (view space: origin = the eye, -Z forward, +Y up): art_model {"action":"create","name":"ar","template":"fp_rifle","textures":{"metal":"gun_metal","polymer":"gun_poly"}}
   Slots: fp_rifle {metal, polymer, magazine, optic, lens}, fp_pistol {metal, slide, polymer, magazine}, fp_arms {sleeve, cuff, glove}. Change parts by name: update {"action":"update","name":"ar","set":{"magazine":{"h":5}}} (also add:[..], remove:["optic"]).
   Arms (3D): create {"action":"create","name":"arms","template":"fp_arms","textures":{"sleeve":"sleeve","glove":"glove"}} (poses rest, grip_rifle, grip_pistol; clip idle_breathe).
3. Clips: fp_rifle has fire, reload_tactical, reload_empty (fp_pistol: fire, reload). Add your own: pose {"action":"pose","name":"ar","pose":"inspect","parts":{"receiver":{"rot":[0,25,-30]}}} then animate {"action":"animate","name":"ar","clip":"inspect","keys":[{"t":0,"pose":"rest"},{"t":0.6,"pose":"inspect","ease":"smooth"},{"t":1.4,"pose":"rest","ease":"smooth"}],"events":[{"t":0.6,"name":"cloth"}]}
   Keys: t in seconds (strictly increasing), pose and/or parts {<node>:{rot:[x,y,z] deg, at:[dx,dy,dz] px in the parent's frame, scale}}; ease = the motion INTO the key (linear | smooth | step). Rotations take the short way: split turns over 180° with an extra key.
4. Check by eye: preview {"action":"preview","name":"ar","clip":"reload_empty","frames":8,"view":"side"} and {"action":"preview","name":"arms","pose":"grip_rifle","views":["fp","side"]}
5a. True 3D: export {"action":"export","name":"ar"} and {"action":"export","name":"arms"} -> one node per part, empty nodes socket_muzzle / socket_sight / socket_grip_r / socket_grip_l / socket_mag_well, one glTF animation per clip (events in extras), meta.json rig table (Roblox Motor6D C0). Parent both to the camera; socket_sight on screen centre for ADS.
5b. 2D sprites (PS1 technique): one canvas per layer, all with the same size and camera so they stack:
   gun: render {"action":"render","name":"ar","canvas":"ar_reload","clip":"reload_empty","fps":12,"size":[160,120],"camera":"fp","hide":["magazine"],"quantize":{"colors":16,"dither":true},"outline":"#14141a"}
   magazine: render {"action":"render","name":"ar","canvas":"ar_reload_mag","clip":"reload_empty","fps":12,"size":[160,120],"camera":"fp","only":["magazine"]}
   sway / turn frames: render {"action":"render","name":"ar","canvas":"ar_sway","sweep":{"yaw":[-6,6,3],"pitch":[-4,4,2]},"size":[160,120]} (row-major: pitch rows x yaw columns, tag "angles")
   Every frame stores each socket's screen anchor [x, y, rot] in the canvas meta.anchors. The fp camera drops (does not clip) triangles crossing the near plane, so a part reaching behind the eye (a long stock) can vanish: shorten it, move the gun forward, or use camera:"side".
6. 2D arms that follow the gun: an art_rig with the render's frame size and one chain per arm (shoulders at the bottom edge):
   art_rig {"action":"create","name":"arms2d","frame":[160,120],"views":["side"],"root":[80,119],"parts":{"body":{"w":2,"h":2,"pivot":[1,1]},"upper_r":{"w":8,"h":32,"pivot":[4,0],"parent":"body","at":[68,0]},"fore_r":{"w":7,"h":30,"pivot":[3,0],"parent":"upper_r","at":[0,30]},"hand_r":{"w":8,"h":8,"pivot":[4,0],"parent":"fore_r","at":[0,28]},"upper_l":{"w":8,"h":32,"pivot":[4,0],"parent":"body","at":[-30,0]},"fore_l":{"w":7,"h":30,"pivot":[3,0],"parent":"upper_l","at":[0,30]},"hand_l":{"w":8,"h":8,"pivot":[4,0],"parent":"fore_l","at":[0,28]}}}
   Draw each part in the cells the reply lists (canvas arms2d_parts, layer "parts"; cell = [x, cells.rows.side, w, h] from cells.parts[part] = [x, w, h]), then:
   art_rig {"action":"animate","name":"arms2d","animation":"reload_empty","canvas":"arms_reload","ik_from":{"canvas":"ar_reload","animation":"reload_empty","map":{"hand_r":{"anchor":"socket_grip_r","bend":-1},"hand_l":"socket_grip_l"}}}
   Same frame count, timing and loop as the gun clip, with the hands solved onto the grips in every frame. Map value: "<anchor>" or {anchor, bend?, rot?:true|deg, at?:[dx,dy], weight?}; offset:[dx,dy] when the frames differ. A humanoid / humanoid_hd rig maps hand_f and hand_b.
7. Paint over any frame by hand, then art_animation {"canvas":"ar_reload","action":"export","format":"spritesheet"} for each layer (json frames[].anchors line the layers up in-engine).

### Skill: prop-rig

Description: Rigs a 3D prop with rigid moving parts (door, chest lid, turret, lever, drawbridge): named parts, pivots, poses and clips, exported as an animated .glb. Use for any hinged or rotating prop that needs no skinning. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Rigid prop rig: doors, chests, turrets, levers (named parts, pivots, poses, clips -> animated .glb)
When: A 3D prop with moving parts and no skinning: a door or gate on a hinge, a chest lid, a turret that yaws and pitches, a lever, a drawbridge. Exported as glTF nodes + animations (in Roblox: one MeshPart per node + Motor6D).

1. Parts: name a part to make it its own node (own mesh); parent nests it (children follow the parent). pivot:[x,y,z] (part-local px; most builders have their origin at the bottom centre) is the JOINT the node rotates about: a lid's back edge, a door's hinge side. Unnamed parts merge into their named parent (latches, rivets) or the root mesh. origin:"bottom" for a standalone prop. Texture canvases must exist first (or use color).
