   art_model {"action":"create","name":"chest","origin":"bottom","parts":[{"type":"box","name":"base","w":16,"h":10,"d":10,"texture":"wood"},{"type":"box","name":"lid","parent":"base","w":16,"h":4,"d":10,"texture":"wood","at":[0,10,0],"pivot":[0,0,-5]},{"type":"box","parent":"lid","w":2,"h":2,"d":1,"color":"#d9b44a","at":[0,10,5]}],"sockets":{"loot":{"part":"base","at":[0,8,0],"look":[0,1,0]}}}
   Turret: base cylinder (root mesh) > box name:"yaw" > box name:"pitch" (parent yaw, pivot at its centre) > cylinder name:"barrel" (parent pitch, rotate:[90,0,0]) + sockets:{muzzle:{part:"barrel", at, look:[0,0,1]}}. Door: frame > leaf with pivot:[-w/2,0,0]. rig:{merge:false} = every part its own node.
2. Poses = offsets from rest per node (rot deg X then Y then Z about the joint, at px in the parent's frame, scale): art_model {"action":"pose","name":"chest","pose":"open","parts":{"lid":{"rot":[-105,0,0]}}}. base:"<pose>" starts from another pose.
3. Clips: art_model {"action":"animate","name":"chest","clip":"open","keys":[{"t":0,"pose":"rest"},{"t":0.15,"parts":{"lid":{"rot":[-8,0,0]}},"ease":"step"},{"t":0.6,"pose":"open","ease":"smooth"}],"events":[{"t":0.15,"name":"unlock"},{"t":0.6,"name":"lid_thud"}]}
   Loops: {"action":"animate","name":"turret","clip":"scan","loop":true,"duration":4,"keys":[{"t":0,"parts":{"yaw":{"rot":[0,-45,0]}}},{"t":2,"parts":{"yaw":{"rot":[0,45,0]}},"ease":"smooth"}]} (a duration past the last key closes back on the first key). keys:null deletes a clip; pose with parts:null deletes a pose.
4. Check: art_model {"action":"preview","name":"chest","clip":"open","frames":4,"view":"side"} (view iso | front | side | {pos, look, fov}); info lists nodes, sockets, poses and clips. The prop is baked onto one atlas canvas chest_uv (contact AO where the lid meets the base, edge wear); paint it on its "paint" layer, and every node keeps using it when posed or exported (unwrap:false = per-part textures).
5. Export: art_model {"action":"export","name":"chest"} -> one node per named part, socket_<name> empty nodes, one glTF animation per clip (all-linear = LINEAR, all-step = STEP, otherwise baked at 30 fps; events in extras), meta.json rig table with parent-space transforms. Play clips by name in-engine.
6. Optional 2D: render {"action":"render","name":"turret","canvas":"turret_scan","clip":"scan","fps":8,"size":[48,48],"camera":"iso","outline":"#14141a"} gives pixel sprite frames with per-frame socket anchors (e.g. where to draw the muzzle flash).

### Skill: ui-icons

Description: Makes a consistent set of pixel-art UI, inventory or ability icons and HUD elements with a shared palette and light direction. Use when asked for an icon set or HUD art. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# UI icons / item icons set
When: Inventory icons, ability icons, HUD elements.

1. Project with a shared palette; 16x16 or 24x24 canvases, 1px transparent margin.
2. Same light direction, outline color and ramp structure for every icon (consistency beats detail).
3. Silhouette -> shade -> outline -> one bright highlight pixel cluster.
4. art_sheet {project} to compare the set; art_critique each.

### Skill: sfx-pack

Description: Generates game sound effects with seeded variants (gore, hits, gunshots, reloads, lasers, explosions, UI clicks, monsters, footsteps) and checks them with analysis images and critiques you can read (art_audio). Use when asked for SFX, sound effects or a sound pack. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Sound-effect pack with variants (gore, combat, holy, UI, monsters, FPS firearms, sci-fi)
When: Game SFX: hits, gore, weapons, gunshots, reloads, lasers, explosions, bells, UI clicks, level-up, roars, footsteps; N variants each.

1. One call per sound, 3 variants each (different seeds = different takes):
   art_audio {"action":"sfx","recipe":"gib_burst","seed":1,"variants":3}
   Other recipes: gib_burst flesh_squelch bone_crunch blood_splat dismember arterial_spray hit_light hit_heavy crit whip_crack blade_swing crossbow_shot censer_whoosh explosion fire_burst bell_toll choir_hit chant_swell click hover confirm level_up monster_growl boss_roar gunshot_rifle gunshot_pistol gunshot_revolver gunshot_marksman gunshot_shotgun gunshot_smg.
2. Shape with vars (same seed = same take): {"action":"sfx","recipe":"bone_crunch","seed":4,"variants":3,"vars":{"pitch":-3,"length":1.2,"intensity":0.9,"wet":0.5}}
3. LOOK at each: art_audio {"action":"analyze","name":"gib_burst_1"} (spectrogram: gore = broadband burst + low thump + wet squelch band 300-1500 Hz; UI = short, mid/high only).
4. art_audio {"action":"critique","name":"gib_burst_1"} -> fix head_silence / too_long / sub_heavy / harsh with vars or fx, re-run step 1 with the same seed.
5. Custom layered sound: {"action":"sfx","name":"censer_hit","layers":[{"kind":"recipe","recipe":"censer_whoosh"},{"kind":"recipe","recipe":"hit_heavy","at":0.45},{"kind":"note","instrument":"church_bells","note":"e4","at":0.45,"gain":-12}],"reverb":{"preset":"hall","wet":0.15}}
6. FPS / sci-fi: art_audio {"action":"sfx","recipe":"gunshot_rifle","variants":4,"vars":{"environment":"indoor","intensity":0.8}} (gunshot_pistol|marksman|shotgun|smg|lmg|suppressed; environment outdoor|indoor|canyon). Handling: mag_out mag_in bolt_rack dry_fire shotgun_pump casing_drop; footstep vars.surface metal|dirt|concrete|snow|grate. Sci-fi: laser_bolt plasma_shot shield_hit glitch_tear teleport_swell servo hologram_ui radio_squelch_on/_off bullet_whiz ricochet; loops: {"action":"sfx","name":"hum","recipe":"drone_rotor","loop":true} (also alarm_klaxon).
   Own sci-fi layers: {"action":"sfx","name":"zap","layers":[{"kind":"glide","pts":[[0,2400],[0.25,300]],"dur":0.3},{"kind":"glitch","at":0.05,"dur":0.2,"gain":-9}],"fx":["dc",{"comp":{"ratio":4}}],"target":-3}. fx, reverb {preset, wet}, target, loop and tail work on recipes and layers alike; info {name} on a recipe asset shows resolved layers to edit.
7. Batch export: art_audio {"action":"export","name":"gib_burst_*","format":"ogg","path":"sfx/gore/"} (also wav 16/24-bit; JSON sidecars hold seed+recipe).

### Skill: music-track

Description: Composes a loopable game music track in any genre with the art_audio notation and generators, then checks it against the intent with the listener report and critique. Use when asked for background music, a boss theme, ambience or a song. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Loopable game music track (any genre), checked with the listener report
When: Background music, boss themes, ambience; anything with tempo, sections and instruments.

1. Pick the genre profile and read its needs: art_help {"topic":"music"} (GENRE RECIPES). Copy the worked cathedral-doom text if it fits.
2. Generate parts you can edit: art_audio {"action":"generate","generator":"doom_riff","style":"chug","key":"e phrygian","bars":2,"seed":4} (also organ_progression, blast_beat, dread_ambient).
3. Write the song (text or JSON, or both: JSON tracks/buses/master deep-merge over the text, so keep notes in text and put fx/gain/bus tweaks in JSON), with intent + genre so critique can check them:
   art_audio {"action":"song","name":"boss","intent":"brutal fast boss fight, blast beats, choir","genre":"death_metal","tempo":180,"key":"e phrygian","loop":true,"tracks":{"gtr":{"instrument":"metal_guitar"},"bass":{"instrument":"bass_guitar","root_only":true},"drums":{"instrument":"metal_kit"},"choir":{"instrument":"choir_pad"}},"sections":{"a":{"bars":4,"gtr":{"gen":"doom_riff","style":"tremolo","seed":2},"bass":{"gen":"doom_riff","style":"tremolo","seed":2},"drums":{"gen":"blast_beat","style":"blast"},"choir":"Em | F | G | F"}},"arrangement":["a","a"]}
4. art_audio {"action":"analyze","name":"boss"}: read "report" first (what a listener hears), then perception.rhythm (felt BPM, kick pattern), genre.verdict, mix.masking.
5. art_audio {"action":"critique","name":"boss"}: fix the top issues (most audible first). Typical: intent_gap -> change drum style/tempo/instrument; masking -> eq carve; buried -> +gain; repetitive -> vary seeds/sections; arrangement -> contrast sections.
   Text + JSON example: art_audio {"action":"song","name":"boss","text":"<the text>","tracks":{"gtr":{"gain":-4,"fx":[{"type":"eq","bands":[{"type":"peak","f":400,"gain":-3}]}]}},"buses":{"drums":{"fx":[{"type":"comp","ratio":4}]}}}
6. Re-send the song (same name) and repeat 4-5 until the report matches the intent. Then export {"action":"export","name":"boss","format":"ogg","stems":true} or layers:true for adaptive music; add sample_rate:48000 for 48 kHz delivery (loop points stay sample-exact).

### Skill: planets-space

Description: Bakes pixel-art planets (orbit maps, LOD meshes, clouds, rings, atmosphere), star systems, matching landing-zone terrain, asteroid fields, nebula skyboxes and space FX sprites for three.js or Roblox (art_planet). Use for planets, space backdrops or alien ground terrain. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Planets, ground terrain and space backdrops (art_planet)
When: Planets seen from orbit and landed on, star systems, landing-zone terrain, rocks and colony anchors, asteroid fields, nebula skyboxes, sun / flare / storm sprites for a browser (three.js) or Roblox game.

1. Pick the system first: art_planet {"action":"system","seed":11,"count":6} and read the strip (one biome each, distinct palettes). Keep names original.
2. Bake each world: art_planet {"action":"planet","name":"kethra","preset":"bloom","seed":7,"hue":-6,"equirect":1024,"face":256}. Look at the orbit image; iterate on biomes / ramps / sea_level / clouds before going bigger.
   Same palette as your project: palette:"project:<name>" (dither stays ordered).
3. In three.js: GLTFLoader the .glb; THREE.LOD from <name>_lods children (userData.distance); swap <name>_atmosphere's material for:
   [code: section "atmosphere"]
   City lights (night side only):
   [code: section "night"]
4. Close approach: stream quadtree tiles (index <name>.tiles.json) instead of LOD0:
   [code: section "quadtree"]
5. Far away (a few px): the disc sprite (<name>_disc.png) or:
   [code: section "impostor"]
6. Landing zone: art_planet {"action":"terrain","planet":"kethra","lat":12,"lon":30,"size":512}. The patch base elevation and colours come from the same planet field (orbit and ground match). Use anchors (landing_pad, mesa_top, arch) to place colony modules. Look at the overview / eye / wide renders; set scene.fog from meta.fog and add the horizon ring.
   [code: section "terrain"]
   Pixel ground detail everywhere near the camera (instead of only the detail decals):
   [code: section "ground"]
7. Space: skybox (scene.background = new THREE.CubeTextureLoader().load([px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz]) with NearestFilter, or the equirect with EquirectangularReflectionMapping), asteroids (field glb is GPU-instanced per variant and LOD; the LOD1+ nodes (userData.lod > 0) are in the file too, so set them visible = false on load or show one level by camera distance), fx sprites (additive planes).
8. Roblox later: every texture is <= 1024 px; meshes per chunk / tile stay well under 20k triangles; Sky faces map px->Rt, nx->Lf, py->Up, ny->Dn, pz->Ft, nz->Bk; heightfield.json can drive Terrain:WriteVoxels or a MeshPart grid; instanced props become cloned MeshParts from scatter.json.

[code: atmosphere]
// three.js (r150+): atmosphere shell for <name>_atmosphere (params: <name>.planet.json -> atmosphere)
const A = meta.atmosphere; // {shell_radius, color, sunset, density, falloff, terminator}
const atmoMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  transparent: true, depthWrite: false, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, side: THREE.FrontSide,
  uniforms: { uSun: { value: new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0) }, uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(...A.color) }, uSunset: { value: new THREE.Color(...A.sunset) },
              uDensity: { value: A.density }, uFalloff: { value: A.falloff }, uTerm: { value: new THREE.Vector2(...A.terminator) } },
  vertexShader: `varying vec3 vN; varying vec3 vV;
    void main() { vec4 w = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0); vN = normalize(mat3(modelMatrix) * normal);
      vV = normalize(cameraPosition - w.xyz); gl_Position = projectionMatrix * viewMatrix * w; }`,
  fragmentShader: `uniform vec3 uSun, uColor, uSunset; uniform float uDensity, uFalloff; uniform vec2 uTerm;
    varying vec3 vN; varying vec3 vV;
    void main() {
      float rim = pow(1.0 - max(dot(vN, vV), 0.0), uFalloff) * uDensity;     // fresnel rim
      float ndl = dot(vN, normalize(uSun));
      float day = smoothstep(uTerm.x, uTerm.y, ndl);                           // day / night terminator
      vec3 col = mix(uColor, uSunset, 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.45, abs(ndl))); // warm band at the terminator
      col = floor(col * rim * day * 6.0 + 0.5) / 6.0;                           // banded: PSX / pixel look
      gl_FragColor = vec4(col, 1.0);
    }`,
});
gltf.scene.getObjectByName(name + '_atmosphere').material = atmoMat; // uSun = sun direction in world space

[code: night]
// night-side city lights (<name>_night.png or cube/<face>_night.png): emissive only where N.L < 0
mat.onBeforeCompile = (s) => {
  s.uniforms.uNight = { value: nightTex }; s.uniforms.uSun = { value: sunDir };
  s.fragmentShader = 'uniform sampler2D uNight; uniform vec3 uSun;\n' + s.fragmentShader.replace('#include <emissivemap_fragment>',
    '#include <emissivemap_fragment>\n float nd = 1.0 - smoothstep(-0.2, 0.05, dot(normalize(vNormal), normalize((viewMatrix * vec4(uSun, 0.0)).xyz)));\n totalEmissiveRadiance += texture2D(uNight, vMapUv).rgb * nd;');
};
nightTex.magFilter = nightTex.minFilter = THREE.NearestFilter;

[code: quadtree]
// quadtree streaming of tiles/<face>/<level>/<x>_<y>.glb (index: <name>.tiles.json)
const idx = await (await fetch(base + name + '.tiles.json')).json();
const byId = new Map(idx.tiles.map((t) => [t.id, t])), loaded = new Map(), loader = new GLTFLoader();
const K = renderer.domElement.height / (2 * Math.tan(THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(camera.fov) / 2));
function want(t, camLocal, out) {                       // camLocal = camera position in planet space
  const d = Math.max(1e-3, camLocal.distanceTo(new THREE.Vector3(...t.center)) - t.radius);
  const sse = t.error * K / d;                          // screen-space error in px
  if (sse <= 1 || !t.children.length) out.push(t.id); else for (const c of t.children) want(byId.get(c), camLocal, out);
}
function update() {
  const camLocal = planet.worldToLocal(camera.position.clone()), ids = [];
  for (const r of idx.roots) want(byId.get(r), camLocal, ids);
  for (const id of ids) if (!loaded.has(id)) { loaded.set(id, null); loader.load(base + byId.get(id).file, (g) => { loaded.set(id, g.scene); planet.add(g.scene); }); }
  for (const [id, obj] of loaded) if (obj) obj.visible = ids.includes(id);   // keep parents until children arrive in a real build
}
// equal-level tiles share edges exactly; skirts (tiles[].skirt) cover the gap next to a tile one level coarser

[code: impostor]
// far planet: camera-facing quad that ray-traces a sphere and samples the equirect albedo
const farMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({ transparent: true, uniforms: { uMap: { value: albedoTex }, uSun: { value: sunDir } },
  vertexShader: `varying vec2 vUv; void main() { vUv = uv * 2.0 - 1.0;
    gl_Position = projectionMatrix * (modelViewMatrix * vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0) + vec4(position.xy, 0.0, 0.0)); }`,
  fragmentShader: `uniform sampler2D uMap; uniform vec3 uSun; varying vec2 vUv;
    void main() { float r2 = dot(vUv, vUv); if (r2 > 1.0) discard;
      vec3 n = vec3(vUv, sqrt(1.0 - r2));                    // view-space sphere normal
      vec3 d = transpose(mat3(viewMatrix)) * n;              // world direction (rotation is orthonormal; add planet spin here)
      vec2 uv = vec2(atan(d.z, d.x) / 6.2831853 + 0.5, asin(clamp(d.y, -1.0, 1.0)) / 3.1415927 + 0.5);
      vec3 c = texture2D(uMap, uv).rgb * (0.05 + 0.95 * max(dot(d, normalize(uSun)), 0.0));
      gl_FragColor = vec4(c, 1.0); }`,
});  // quad side = 2 * radius; or just billboard <name>_disc.png (pre-lit) past impostor.switch_distance

[code: terrain]
// ground patch: chunks + props + heightfield for physics
for (const c of meta.chunk_files) loader.load(base + c.file, (g) => {
  const lods = new THREE.LOD();
  for (const n of g.scene.getObjectByName(`chunk_${c.x}_${c.z}_lods`).children) lods.addLevel(n, n.userData.distance);
  g.scene.getObjectByName(`chunk_${c.x}_${c.z}_collision`).visible = false;   // physics mesh
  scene.add(lods);
});
loader.load(base + name + '_props.glb', (g) => scene.add(g.scene));    // EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing -> InstancedMesh
for (const d of meta.detail_files) loader.load(base + d.file, (g) => { g.scene.traverse((o) => { if (o.material) { o.material.polygonOffset = true; o.material.polygonOffsetFactor = -1; } }); scene.add(g.scene); });
if (meta.horizon) loader.load(base + meta.horizon.file, (g) => scene.add(g.scene));    // ring out to the far ranges
scene.fog = new THREE.FogExp2(meta.fog.color, meta.fog.density);         // sky: gradient meta.fog.sky.horizon -> zenith
const hf = await (await fetch(base + name + '.heightfield.json')).json();
const heightAt = (x, z) => { const i = Math.round((x + hf.size_m / 2) / hf.spacing_m), j = Math.round((z + hf.size_m / 2) / hf.spacing_m);
  return hf.heights[j * (hf.grid + 1) + i]; };                             // or feed hf.heights to a physics heightfield

[code: ground]
// near-ground pixel detail at any distance (same rules as the baked chunk / detail textures):
// splat (LinearFilter), tileset atlas + masks + noise (NearestFilter, RepeatWrapping)
const groundMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({ uniforms: { uSplat: { value: splat }, uAtlas: { value: atlas }, uMask: { value: masks }, uNoise: { value: noise },
    uSize: { value: meta.size_m }, uTileM: { value: meta.ground.tile_m }, uNoiseP: { value: meta.ground.noise.period_m } },
  vertexShader: `varying vec3 vW; void main() { vec4 w = modelMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0); vW = w.xyz; gl_Position = projectionMatrix * viewMatrix * w; }`,
  fragmentShader: `uniform sampler2D uSplat, uAtlas, uMask, uNoise; uniform float uSize, uTileM, uNoiseP; varying vec3 vW;
    void main() {
      vec2 nz = texture2D(uNoise, vW.xz / uNoiseP).rg - 0.5;
      vec4 w = texture2D(uSplat, (vW.xz + nz * 5.0) / uSize + 0.5);                 // noise-perturbed splat lookup
      float ws[4] = float[4](w.r, w.g, w.b, w.a); int A = 0, B = 1;
      for (int i = 1; i < 4; i++) if (ws[i] > ws[A]) A = i;
      B = A == 0 ? 1 : 0; for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) if (i != A && ws[i] > ws[B]) B = i;
      float t = ws[B] / max(ws[A] + ws[B], 1e-4);
      vec2 tuv = fract(vW.xz / uTileM);                                               // one tile per tile_m metres
      float m = texture2D(uMask, vec2(tuv.x, (tuv.y + float(B)) / 4.0)).r;
      int L = m < t ? B : A;                                                          // organic, noise-masked border
      float variant = floor(texture2D(uNoise, vW.xz / (uNoiseP * 2.0)).r * 3.99);
      vec2 auv = vec2((variant + tuv.x) / 6.0, (float(L) + tuv.y) / 4.0);            // atlas: 6 columns x 4 layers
      gl_FragColor = vec4(texture2D(uAtlas, auv).rgb, 1.0);                         // + lighting / fog chunks as usual
    }`,
});  // swap it in for the chunks within ~64 m of the camera; keep the baked textures beyond

### Skill: combat-fx

Description: Makes seeded pixel-art combat effect flipbooks (muzzle flashes, tracers, casings, impacts, decals, explosions, smoke, fire, sparks, steam) with engine metadata for three.js or Roblox (art_fx). Use when asked for muzzle flashes, hit effects, explosions or other VFX sprites. Uses the Agent Art MCP tools (art_*).

# Combat visual effects for a pixel-art shooter (art_fx)
When: Muzzle flashes, tracers, casings, bullet impacts and decals, explosions, smoke, fire, sparks, alarms for a browser (three.js) or Roblox FPS / TPS with pixel-art sprites.

1. Lock the look first: art_fx {"action":"make","type":"muzzle","variant":"rifle","view":"side","seed":3} and {"action":"make","type":"impact","variant":"metal"}. Shift hue (hue:-8 warmer) or palette:"project:<name>" so effects share the game palette.
2. Whole set in one call: {"action":"batch","preset":"all","seed":3,"group":"combat"} -> read <group>_contact.png; remake single effects with another seed or size where they read badly at game scale (impacts must read at 1-2 px per detail in a 384x216 frame).
3. First person: render the gun with art_model render {camera:"fp", size:[384,216]} (socket_muzzle per frame), then {"action":"preview","type":"muzzle","variant":"rifle","over":{"canvas":"ar_fire","anchor":"socket_muzzle"}}; make the fp variant with the same anchor / aim_deg for the game.
4. Pair sounds: each entry's sound list = art_audio sfx recipes (gunshot_rifle, ricochet, explosion ...). Pair lights: entry.light drives a point light per frame.
5. {"action":"export","group":"combat"} -> combat.fx.json (validated). Load it with the snippet in art_help {topic:"fx"}; Roblox notes there too.
